articles.summary: CNN’s John Berman examines the difference in the MLB fan experience in America and Japan. CNN Films new “Homecoming: The Tokyo Series” explores how baseball became a profound cultural tradition shaped by ritual, discipline and devotion. Stream it now on the CNN app.
articles.body:
CNN's John Berman examines the difference in the MLB fan experience in America and Japan. CNN Films new “Homecoming: The Tokyo Series” explores how baseball became a profound cultural tradition shaped by ritual, discipline and devotion. Stream it now on the CNN app.

Videos showing a person dressed up as Cat in the Hat roaming streets after dark have spread across social media, even prompting responses from police in Ireland and the UK. But it remains unclear which, if any, of the sightings are real or if they are AI-generated.

Kirk Heilbrun, a psychologist called by the prosecution , testified that he concluded Lindsay Clancy was not psychotic when she killed her three children and understood her actions were wrong. Helibrun told the court his "clinical opinion is that she was criminally responsible on January 24th." Defense attorneys for Clancy, who is charged with murder, argue she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and extreme mental illness and should not be held criminally responsible for the killings.

Justin Lester, a pastor in Vallejo, California created an "AI twin" so his constituents could have access to him 24/7. CNN's Nick Watt speaks to him about how it works.

Target is facing backlash for selling a children’s Halloween costume depicting a circus clown that critics said evoked blackface and minstrel shows. The company announced it pulled the item and acknowledged the issue in an apology.

Natalie Harp’s now-inactive Twitter feed shows a non-stop thread of posts showing devotion to President Donald Trump. These posts were on her account years before she became a White House aide to the president, posting more than 150 tweets on January 6, 2021, alone, in support of the president. CNN's Isabelle Chapman reports.

Capybaras, penguins and even giant snails were weighed and measured as London Zoo carried out its annual health checks. The data helps keep track of the animals’ health and contributes to a global conservation database.

Divine, a new app inspired by six-second video platform Vine, launched last week and already has about 100,000 users, according to its founder. CNN’s Matias Grez looks at what you can do on the app and how it stands apart from other mainstream social media platforms. Divine is not formally affiliated with Vine.

articles.title: MLB Umpire Jordan Baker Hit in Face Mask by Foul Ball, In Concussion Protocol After Leaving Game
articles.summary: An MLB umpire is in concussion protocol after a baseball hit his face mask on Tuesday during a matchup between the San Francisco Giants and Cleveland Guardians.
articles.body:
An MLB umpire is in concussion protocol after a baseball hit his face mask on Tuesday during a matchup between the San Francisco Giants and Cleveland Guardians.

San Francisco's Andrew Knizner hit a foul ball that hit home plate umpire Jordan Baker in his mask, and he was forced to exit the game. According to the Associated Press , MLB said in a statement that Baker was being evaluated for a concussion.

Rob Drake had to move from third base to home plate, which led to a 12-minute delay in the game. Steven Jaschinski moved from second to third and Stu Scheurwater remained at third as the game was played with a three-man crew the rest of the night.

According to the Associated Press, MLB will determine Baker's status overnight and decide whether to bring in another umpire for the rest of the series. The Guardians won Tuesday's game, and the two teams will play on Wednesday and Thursday.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani Reaches Another HR Milestone, Latest Box Score Stats & Highlights from Dodgers-Rockies
articles.summary: When healthy, Shohei Ohtani is one of the best pitchers in baseball.
articles.body:
When healthy, Shohei Ohtani is one of the best pitchers in baseball.

Turns out, he can do a little bit of hitting as well.

The Los Angeles Dodgers star launched a two-run homer in the third inning of Tuesday's contest against the Colorado Rockies. It was his 30th of the season and marked the sixth straight year he reached the milestone.

Here is a look at Ohtani's box score stats from the contest:

The Dodgers held on to defeat the Rockies 7-6 with Tanner Scott getting the save one day after Edwin Díaz, who was placed on the IL before Tuesday's game, got hit around again.

Ohtani's Dodgers (76-51) are still a comfortable eight games ahead of the San Diego Padres in the National League West, but they are just 7-10 in August even after winning the first two games in Colorado.

They surely want to bounce back and hit their stride before the playoffs, and the future Hall of Famer continuing to hit at such a level is an important part of that. In fact, it is even more important because he hasn't pitched since July 3 because of injury concerns.

The lack of pitching means his impact is limited to his bat.

Fortunately for the Dodgers, it is arguably the best one in the league.

The two-way star has four MVPs and four Silver Sluggers on his illustrious resume. This is his third year with the Dodgers, and all he did in each of his first two was help lead the team to a World Series title as the National League MVP.

He led the league in home runs in back-to-back years in 2023 (44) and 2024 (54) and then launched a career-high 55 long balls last season. While he likely won't reach that 55 mark in 2026 barring an incredible closing stretch, he has still shown off his incredible power with 30.

Ohtani also hit two home runs in Los Angeles' victory over the Rockies on Monday as he battles Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong for this year's NL MVP.

A few more swings like the one he unleashed Tuesday could provide him just the boost he needs in that race.

articles.title: Jo Adell Sets Career High RBI, Final Box Score Stats and Updated AL Standings After Guardians Win
articles.summary: Every win is critically important in the crowded American League wild-card race, and Jo Adell led the Cleveland Guardians to a commanding one Tuesday.
articles.body:
Every win is critically important in the crowded American League wild-card race, and Jo Adell led the Cleveland Guardians to a commanding one Tuesday.

Adell tallied three hits, including a home run, on his way to a career-high six RBI in Cleveland's 8-1 victory over the San Francisco Giants. Joe Reedy of the Associated Press noted the three-run homer traveled 455 feet in the first inning, which helped set the tone.

Here is a look at his box score stats and where the Guardians fit in the AL playoff race:

While it was largely a one-man show in the RBI department for Cleveland, third baseman José Ramírez added three hits as well.

It was a much-needed win for the Guardians, who have struggled with consistency of late and entered Tuesday's contest just 9-19 since the All-Star break. It has fallen behind in the AL Central as a result but is just one bounce-back stretch from reestablishing itself as a wild-card team.

Perhaps Tuesday was the start of that bounce-back effort.

If it was, it could start with Adell also turning things around. After all, he was just 7-for-42 (.167) since joining the Guardians ahead of the Aug. 4 trade deadline prior to Tuesday's breakthrough effort.

Cleveland acquired him from the Los Angeles Angels to add his power to the lineup. He launched 16 home runs in 111 games with the Angels before the trade and is just one season removed from his career-high 37 in 2025.

Having him return to that form would be quite the boost for a lineup that largely relies on Ramírez and Steven Kwan to lead the way.

Adell and the Guardians will look to clinch a series-win over the Giants on Wednesday at 6:40 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Brewers Make MLB History in 22-0 Win vs. Mariners, Final Box Score Stats and Highlights from Shutout
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers have the best record in baseball, and they show no signs of cooling off as the postseason nears.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers have the best record in baseball, and they show no signs of cooling off as the postseason nears.

On Tuesday, the Brewers beat the Seattle Mariners 22-0, tying the largest shutout win since the start of 1888. It's the largest shutout since Cleveland beat the New York Yankees by the same score.

Milwaukee didn't exactly get off to a hot start, as it scored just one run through the first four innings, and it came on an error. The offense exploded in the fifth inning, however.

Jackson Chourio hit an RBI single, William Contreras hit a sac fly and Christian Yelich delivered a three-run homer to make it a 6-0 lead.

David Hamilton opened up the sixth inning with a three-run homer, and Jake Bauers tacked on two more runs with another home run to increase the lead to 11 runs.

Hamilton delivered an RBI single in the bottom of the seventh before another run scored on a fielder's choice. Things got even more out of hand in the eighth when Luis Lara hit a three-run home run to make it 16-0. It was the first homer of his career.

The Brewers tacked on six more runs in the eighth to get to 22 runs.

On the mound, Milwaukee's Kyle Harrison picked up the win after striking out eight and giving up just two hits in five innings. Seattle's Bryce Miller was credited with the loss as he allowed six runs and a home run.

The Mariners went to Josh Simpson in the fifth inning and Nick Davila in the sixth and seventh innings before waiving the white flag and putting third basemen Leo Rivas on the mound in the eighth.

The Brewers are sitting comfortably at 78-48 and are on their way to finishing with the best record in baseball. The two teams will meet again on Wednesday, and Seattle can only hope things go differently in the second game of the series.

articles.title: Little League World Series 2026 Wednesday Schedule, TV Info and Bracket Predictions
articles.summary: The 2026 Little League World Series kicks off Wednesday in Williamsport, Pennsylvania, with the first action in the United States and International brackets.
articles.body:
The 2026 Little League World Series kicks off Wednesday in Williamsport, Pennsylvania, with the first action in the United States and International brackets.

Seoul, South Korea, takes to the diamond with lofty expectations and championship aspirations. To achieve them, they will have to get past the Canadian representative, Little Mountain Little League, from Vancouver.

What other games are on tap on the opening day of this year's tournament, and how can you watch?

Great Lakes Region: West Side LL (Hamilton, Ohio)

Metro Region: Bayonne Central LL (Bayonne, New Jersey)

Mid-Atlantic Region: East Side LL (West Chester, Pennsylvania)

Midwest Region: Davenport Northwest LL (Davenport, Iowa)

Mountain Region: Paseo Verde, LL (Henderson, Nevada)

New England Region: Bridgewater Joe Lozaro LL (Bridgewater, Massachusetts)

Northwest Region: Soundview LL (Tacoma, Washington)

Southeast Region: Phenix City Youth Baseball LL (Phenix City, Alabama)

Southwest Region: Boerne LL (Boerne, Texas)

West Region: Sweetwater Valley LL (Bonita, California)

Asian-Pacific Region: West Seoul (B) LL (Seoul, South Korea)

Australia Region: Ryde Little League (Sydney, New South Wales)

Canada Region: Little Mountain LLC (Vancouver, British Columbia)

Caribbean Region: Los Nacionales LL (Santiago, Dominican Republic)

Curaçao Region: Pariba LL (Willemstad, Curaçao)

Europe and Africa Region: South Czech Republic LL (Brno, Czechia)

Latin American Region: Ministerio Sobre Las Alas Del Aguila LL (Leon, Nicaragua)

Mexico Region: Municipal De Tijuana LL (Tijuana, Baja California)

Panama Region: David Doleguita LL (Chiriquí, Panama)

Game 1: Latin America vs. Caribbean (1:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: Latin America)

Game 2: Northwest vs. Southeast (3:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: Southeast)

Game 3: Canada vs. Asia-Pacific (5:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: Asia-Pacific)

Game 4: New England vs. Metro (7:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: New England)

Looking Ahead: Can California Win No. 9?

California is the most decorated American state in the Little League Baseball World Series, with eight titles entering the 2026 tournament.

This year's squad, Sweetwater Valley Little League from San Bonita, has the potential to win a ninth title and etch their name in the history books at the same time.

The team defeated Hawaii in the West Region finale back on August 14, scoring 11 runs and sending a message to the rest of the field in the process.

The trip to Williamsport is not a routine one for the Sweetwater Valley team. It has not advanced to this LLWS since 2015, when both of its losses came at the hands of the eventual United States bracket runner-up, Texas.

It remains to be seen if California will add to its lengthy championship resume this year. Still, it will have a chance to get off to a hot start against the Midwest representative from Davenport, Iowa, as part of Thursday's Day Two slate.

articles.title: 10 MLB Stars Who Played in the Little League World Series
articles.summary: Among all the good reasons (fun, etc.) to watch the Little League World Series, you just never know when you might be watching a future major leaguer.
articles.body:
Among all the good reasons (fun, etc.) to watch the Little League World Series, you just never know when you might be watching a future major leaguer.

The Little League World Series has been held in Williamsport, Pennsylvania since 1947. And starting with Jim Barbieri in 1953, dozens of players who have played in the event have gone on to play in Major League Baseball.

The list isn't a "Who's Who" of major league stars for the most part, but it does consist of several future World Series winners, two of the best outfielders in MLB today and a noted slugger of 509 career home runs.

So after beginning with some honorable mentions, let's run through 10 MLB stars who got their starts in the Little League World Series. They are ranked according to their career WAR in the majors.

McClendon, Cash and Wilson have all managed in the big leagues, and Wilson is even a member of the Seattle Mariners' Hall of Fame.

The other name that might stick out here is Charlie Hayes, though not entirely because he played 14 seasons in the majors. He's the father of Ke'Bryan Hayes, a two-time Gold Glove Award winner.

Conforto's career has hit a wall in the 2020s, but he's still a former All-Star with 17.4 career rWAR. That's almost as good as Rasmus, who managed to rack up 20.4 rWAR before retiring after his age-31 season in 2018.

Profar and Schoop were teammates for the Willemstad, Curacao team in 2004. They own a combined 28.6 rWAR and two All-Star selections as big leaguers.

Little League World Series: Willemstad, Curacao in 2012

Like Jurickson Profar and Jonathan Schoop before him, Ceddanne Rafaela got his start with the Willemstad team in the Little League World Series back in 2012. He only went 1-for-9 in the tournament, but made an impression with his Ozzie Smith-style acrobatics .

These days, Rafaela has a case as the best center fielder in the American League.

Last year saw him win his first Gold Glove, and the evolution of his bat has turned him into an All-Star in 2026. His OPS is a career high .796, and he has more extra-base hits than every center fielder except Pete Crow-Armstrong.

Because Rafaela will only turn 26 on September 18, he may only just now be coming into a long and fruitful prime.

Little League World Series: Almonte Springs, Florida in 1984

Jason Varitek occupies a unique place in Little League World Series lore.

As of 2020, he was the only LLWS alum to get elected to the College Baseball Hall of Fame, and one of only three to play in the World Series at the Little League, NCAA and major league levels.

As a major leaguer, he played all 15 of his MLB seasons with the Boston Red Sox and racked up plenty of accolades along the way.

At his peak in 2005, Varitek was an All-Star and a Gold Glove and Silver Slugger Award winner. He also won World Series titles in 2004 and 2007, ultimately hitting 11 home runs in 62 career postseason games.

Among catchers, the latter mark is tied for second all-time after only Yogi Berra.

Little League World Series: Trail, British Columbia in 1990

When Jason Bay repped Canada in the Little League World Series in 1990, it wouldn't be the last time he took the international stage for his native country. He did so again in the inaugural World Baseball Classic in 2006.

In the years after the Little League World Series, Bay was traded three times before he completed his rookie season in 2004. So when he won the NL Rookie of the Year award that year, he achieved something that only Lou Piniella had achieved before him.

During a six-season heyday between 2004 and 2009, Bay's average season consisted of 30 home runs and 99 RBI. He was an All-Star three times, and his 222 major league home runs rank fifth all-time among Canadian-born players.

In 2019, Bay was elected into the Canadian Baseball Hall of Fame .

Little League World Series: Toms River, New Jersey in 1998

Todd Frazier didn't just play in the Little League World Series championship game in 1998. He led off with a home run for Toms River, and later struck out the Japanese team's last hitter to seal the title.

As a major leaguer, Frazier was a bit of a late-bloomer who didn't truly break out until he was in his late 20s. But once he did, he clubbed 131 home runs in a four-year span between 2014 and 2017. That put him in the top 10 for those four seasons.

As a slugger, Frazier's most famous feat is winning the Home Run Derby in 2015. The sugar on top was getting to do it while representing the Cincinnati Reds in their home stadium at Great American Ball Park.

Unless, of course, one considers Frazier's greatest slugging feat to be that time he hit a no-handed home run in 2012.

Little League World Series: Brownsburg, Indiana in 1999

Lance Lynn's run in the Little League World Series in 1999 ended when he gave up a game-ending grand slam. Yet years later, he was still able to look back on the event as an inspiration .

Years later, Lynn was a first-round pick by the St. Louis Cardinals in 2008 and a World Series champion as a rookie in 2011. It was the first of two World Series that he ended up pitching in, putting him in an exclusive club among LLWS alumni.

Apart from that, Lynn is best known for being a workhorse who tallied 2,006.1 innings in his 13 major league seasons. He was an All-Star twice, and he had a run as an annual Cy Young Award contender between 2019 and 2021.

All told, Lynn was 12th among right-handed pitchers in rWAR between 2011 and 2024. The name directly underneath him on that list belongs to none other than Stephen Strasburg.

Little League World Series: Portland, Oregon in 1958

When Rick Wise pitched for the Boston Red Sox in the 1975 World Series, it was technically his third World Series . In addition to the LLWS in 1958, he also pitched in the Babe Ruth World Series in 1961.

No matter which way you slice it, that 1975 season was Wise's big moment in the big leagues. He earned both Cy Young Award and MVP votes, and he was notably the winning pitcher in Game 6 of that year's World Series—as in, the one with the Carlton Fisk home run .

Wise was previously an All-Star in 1971 and 1973, and even an injury-shortened 1974 season only did so much to mar his track record as an innings-eater. Between 1969 and 1976, he averaged 221.1 innings per season.

Wise hung up his spikes in 1982, and he eventually took on a coaching career that lasted until 2008.

Little League World Series: Chandler, Arizona in 2007

Cody Bellinger wasn't the only one making memories during the 2007 Little League World Series. That Chandler, Arizona team was coached by his father , Clay, who had been a two-time World Series champion for the New York Yankees.

In retrospect, how the younger Bellinger was only a fourth-round pick six years later is hard to fathom.

Though he's had to evolve his game over the years, Bellinger has a case as the most decorated player in MLB today. He's been a Rookie of the Year and the MVP of a regular season, a postseason series and an All-Star Game. He also has a Gold Glove and Silver Slugger, not to mention a World Series ring.

All of this is even though Bellinger just turned 30 on July 13.

Little League World Series: Lakeland, Florida in 1954

Boog Powell is the first true major league star to come out of the Little League World Series, and it wasn't even his bat that made him a star in the tournament. At the time, he was a pitcher .

It was ultimately as a slugger that Powell left his mark on Major League Baseball. Between his first homer in 1962 and his last homer in 1976, Powell clubbed 339 home runs. It was the 10th-most for that span, sandwiching him in between Hall of Famers Willie Mays and Carl Yastrzemski.

Powell's peak was between 1964 and 1971, when he had four 30-homer seasons and averaged a 143 OPS+. He was a top-three finisher for the MVP three times, including when he won it in 1970.

That was also the year that Powell carried the Baltimore Orioles to a championship. Between the ALCS and the World Series, he hit .355 with three homers and 11 RBI in eight games.

Little League World Series: Santa Clara, California in 1969

Carney Lansford's Little League World Series team went all the way to the finals in 1969, only to get shut out by the winners from Taiwan by a 5-0 final.

From there, he went on to be a third-round pick in 1975 and one of the better third basemen in MLB during his day. Between 1978 and 1992, only four players racked up more rWAR at the hot corner.

Lansford was a career .290 hitter who twice peaked as a .336 hitter in a given season, and both times had major ramifications. He was the AL batting champion the first time in 1981, and eventually a World Series champion the second time in 1989.

That was the only World Series that Lansford played in, and he made it count. In the then-Oakland Athletics' four-game sweep over the San Francisco Giants, he went 7-for-16 with a homer.

Little League World Series: Tampa, Florida in 1980

Gary Sheffield had never been on a plane before he had to fly to Williamsport for the Little League World Series as an 11-year-old in 1980. He must have shaken off the nerves, because he ended up batting .600 in the series.

And so goes the origin story for one of the great major league careers in living memory.

Sheffield was the No. 6 overall pick in the draft in 1986, and he was an All-Star and MVP contender just six years later in 1992. It was also the first of eight 30-homer seasons between then and 2005. He retired with 509 career home runs in 2009.

Sheffield's perceived ties to performance-enhancing drugs were among several factors that may have affected his Hall of Fame candidacy in his final year on the ballot in 2024. But if nothing else, what nobody can deny him is that he might have the most oft-imitated swing of any right-handed hitter ever.

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .
paragraphs: Among all the good reasons (fun, etc.) to watch the Little League World Series, you just never know when you might be watching a future major leaguer.

The Little League World Series has been held in Williamsport, Pennsylvania since 1947. And starting with Jim Barbieri in 1953, dozens of players who have played in the event have gone on to play in Major League Baseball.

The list isn't a "Who's Who" of major league stars for the most part, but it does consist of several future World Series winners, two of the best outfielders in MLB today and a noted slugger of 509 career home runs.
So after beginning with some honorable mentions, let's run through 10 MLB stars who got their starts in the Little League World Series. They are ranked according to their career WAR in the majors.
McClendon, Cash and Wilson have all managed in the big leagues, and Wilson is even a member of the Seattle Mariners' Hall of Fame.
The other name that might stick out here is Charlie Hayes, though not entirely because he played 14 seasons in the majors. He's the father of Ke'Bryan Hayes, a two-time Gold Glove Award winner.

Conforto's career has hit a wall in the 2020s, but he's still a former All-Star with 17.4 career rWAR. That's almost as good as Rasmus, who managed to rack up 20.4 rWAR before retiring after his age-31 season in 2018.
Profar and Schoop were teammates for the Willemstad, Curacao team in 2004. They own a combined 28.6 rWAR and two All-Star selections as big leaguers.
Little League World Series: Willemstad, Curacao in 2012

Like Jurickson Profar and Jonathan Schoop before him, Ceddanne Rafaela got his start with the Willemstad team in the Little League World Series back in 2012. He only went 1-for-9 in the tournament, but made an impression with his Ozzie Smith-style acrobatics .
These days, Rafaela has a case as the best center fielder in the American League.

Last year saw him win his first Gold Glove, and the evolution of his bat has turned him into an All-Star in 2026. His OPS is a career high .796, and he has more extra-base hits than every center fielder except Pete Crow-Armstrong.
Because Rafaela will only turn 26 on September 18, he may only just now be coming into a long and fruitful prime.
Little League World Series: Almonte Springs, Florida in 1984
Jason Varitek occupies a unique place in Little League World Series lore.
As of 2020, he was the only LLWS alum to get elected to the College Baseball Hall of Fame, and one of only three to play in the World Series at the Little League, NCAA and major league levels.
As a major leaguer, he played all 15 of his MLB seasons with the Boston Red Sox and racked up plenty of accolades along the way.

At his peak in 2005, Varitek was an All-Star and a Gold Glove and Silver Slugger Award winner. He also won World Series titles in 2004 and 2007, ultimately hitting 11 home runs in 62 career postseason games.
Among catchers, the latter mark is tied for second all-time after only Yogi Berra.
Little League World Series: Trail, British Columbia in 1990

When Jason Bay repped Canada in the Little League World Series in 1990, it wouldn't be the last time he took the international stage for his native country. He did so again in the inaugural World Baseball Classic in 2006.

In the years after the Little League World Series, Bay was traded three times before he completed his rookie season in 2004. So when he won the NL Rookie of the Year award that year, he achieved something that only Lou Piniella had achieved before him.

During a six-season heyday between 2004 and 2009, Bay's average season consisted of 30 home runs and 99 RBI. He was an All-Star three times, and his 222 major league home runs rank fifth all-time among Canadian-born players.
In 2019, Bay was elected into the Canadian Baseball Hall of Fame .
Little League World Series: Toms River, New Jersey in 1998

Todd Frazier didn't just play in the Little League World Series championship game in 1998. He led off with a home run for Toms River, and later struck out the Japanese team's last hitter to seal the title.

As a major leaguer, Frazier was a bit of a late-bloomer who didn't truly break out until he was in his late 20s. But once he did, he clubbed 131 home runs in a four-year span between 2014 and 2017. That put him in the top 10 for those four seasons.

As a slugger, Frazier's most famous feat is winning the Home Run Derby in 2015. The sugar on top was getting to do it while representing the Cincinnati Reds in their home stadium at Great American Ball Park.
Unless, of course, one considers Frazier's greatest slugging feat to be that time he hit a no-handed home run in 2012.
Little League World Series: Brownsburg, Indiana in 1999
Lance Lynn's run in the Little League World Series in 1999 ended when he gave up a game-ending grand slam. Yet years later, he was still able to look back on the event as an inspiration .

Years later, Lynn was a first-round pick by the St. Louis Cardinals in 2008 and a World Series champion as a rookie in 2011. It was the first of two World Series that he ended up pitching in, putting him in an exclusive club among LLWS alumni.

Apart from that, Lynn is best known for being a workhorse who tallied 2,006.1 innings in his 13 major league seasons. He was an All-Star twice, and he had a run as an annual Cy Young Award contender between 2019 and 2021.
All told, Lynn was 12th among right-handed pitchers in rWAR between 2011 and 2024. The name directly underneath him on that list belongs to none other than Stephen Strasburg.
Little League World Series: Portland, Oregon in 1958

When Rick Wise pitched for the Boston Red Sox in the 1975 World Series, it was technically his third World Series . In addition to the LLWS in 1958, he also pitched in the Babe Ruth World Series in 1961.

No matter which way you slice it, that 1975 season was Wise's big moment in the big leagues. He earned both Cy Young Award and MVP votes, and he was notably the winning pitcher in Game 6 of that year's World Series—as in, the one with the Carlton Fisk home run .

Wise was previously an All-Star in 1971 and 1973, and even an injury-shortened 1974 season only did so much to mar his track record as an innings-eater. Between 1969 and 1976, he averaged 221.1 innings per season.
Wise hung up his spikes in 1982, and he eventually took on a coaching career that lasted until 2008.
Little League World Series: Chandler, Arizona in 2007

Cody Bellinger wasn't the only one making memories during the 2007 Little League World Series. That Chandler, Arizona team was coached by his father , Clay, who had been a two-time World Series champion for the New York Yankees.
In retrospect, how the younger Bellinger was only a fourth-round pick six years later is hard to fathom.

Though he's had to evolve his game over the years, Bellinger has a case as the most decorated player in MLB today. He's been a Rookie of the Year and the MVP of a regular season, a postseason series and an All-Star Game. He also has a Gold Glove and Silver Slugger, not to mention a World Series ring.
All of this is even though Bellinger just turned 30 on July 13.

articles.title: MLB's Top 25 Most Overpaid Players
articles.summary: Paying a player top dollar is no guarantee that he's going to produce at the level that earned him that payday in the first place, and this season more than ever that seems like a theme across baseball.
articles.body:
Paying a player top dollar is no guarantee that he's going to produce at the level that earned him that payday in the first place, and this season more than ever that seems like a theme across baseball.

With a salary north of $50 million and a 93 OPS+ on the year, Kyle Tucker is the most glaring example this season, but he is far from baseball's only massively overpaid player.

Ahead we've highlighted the 25 most overpaid players in the league, focusing solely on 2026 salary relative to 2026 production.

Players are presented alphabetically, so placement within the article should not be interpreted as a reflection of ranking relative to other players.

Note: Salaries referenced in the article reflect luxury-tax payroll figures, courtesy of Spotrac.

2026 Salary: $26,000,000 Stats: 116 G, 96 OPS+, .224/.285/.413, 45 XBH (19 HR), 48 RBI WAR: 1.6

After a rocky start to his first season in San Francisco, shortstop Willy Adames ultimately rebounded to post a 111 OPS+ with 30 home runs and 3.7 WAR to kick off his seven-year, $182 million deal.

This year, that rebound simply hasn't come, and while he has provided positive value with his glove and extra-base pop, his production has been a far cry from justifying one of the largest salaries of any shortstop.

2026 Salary: $23,333,333 Stats: 38 G, 79 OPS+, .261/.291/.358, 9 XBH (2 HR), 14 RBI WAR: -0.4

Following a surprise return to relevance in 2025 when he earned an All-Star selection and was a 2.0-WAR player, Javier Báez has been limited this season by a severe ankle sprain that cost him nearly three months.

He has started 10 of the last 16 games for Detroit at shortstop, with rookie Kevin McGonigle shifting over to third base when he's in the lineup, but he profiles best as a versatile utility piece in the fifth season of his six-year, $140 million contract.

Stats: 125 G, 95 OPS+, .267/.314/.386, 33 XBH (12 HR), 63 RBI

The Mets signed Bo Bichette to a three-year, $126 million deal with opt-outs after the 2026 and 2027 seasons. Early reports portrayed him as a potential opt-out candidate, but that now appears unlikely.

While he is still only 28 years old, Bichette is struggling through the worst offensive season of his career outside of an injury-plagued 2024 campaign. The shift to third base has gone relatively smoothly (-2 DRS, 3 OAA), but his bat has always been what drives his value and it has not even been league average.

2026 Salary: $26,000,000 Stats: Injured, has not played WAR: N/A

"My focus has just been to find stuff that helps me wake up each day in hopefully a little less pain than the day before," Kris Bryant told reporters during spring training when asked about when he might return to the field.

Diagnosed with chronic lumbar degenerative disk disease, Bryant has played 170 total games over the first five seasons in Colorado, including 11 last year and zero this season. The 2016 NL MVP has two years and $52 million left on the books when the 2026 season ends.

2026 Salary: $32,910,744 Stats: Injured, has not played WAR: N/A

When healthy, Corbin Burnes pitched well during his first season with the D-backs, posting a 2.66 ERA in 64.1 innings over 11 starts. However, his season was cut short with an elbow injury that led to Tommy John surgery, and he has not taken the mound since June 1, 2025.

He was building up for a potential return when he suffered a shoulder strain in June, but he has resumed throwing and is now eyeing a potential September comeback. Can the 2021 NL Cy Young winner be a factor in Arizona's playoff push?

2026 Salary: $28,333,333 Stats: 6 GS, 6.30 ERA, 1.47 WHIP, 11 BB, 37 K, 30.0 IP WAR: -0.6

Garrett Crochet was every bit the ace the Red Sox hoped they were acquiring in his first season in Boston, posting a 2.59 ERA with 255 strikeouts in 205.1 innings to finish runner-up in AL Cy Young voting.

After a few early duds, including a brutal start against the Twins on April 13 (1.2 IP, 9 H, 3 BB, 10 ER), he was shelved with shoulder inflammation. What was originally expected to be a brief IL stint has stretched nearly four months, as he developed a lat strain while ramping back up and could now be out the rest of the year.

2026 Salary: $21,120,000 Stats: 16 G, 7/11 SV, 11.85 ERA, 2.56 WHIP, 13.2 IP WAR: -1.4

Edwin Díaz was utterly dominant last season for the Mets, posting a 1.63 ERA and 13.3 K/9 with 28 saves in 62 appearances before opting out of his contract and inking a new three-year, $69 million deal with the Dodgers.

After struggling to a 10.50 ERA over his first seven appearances with reduced fastball velocity, he was sidelined with arm fatigue and underwent arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies. He returned on July 29, but has three blown saves in six chances since returning.

2026 Salary: $18,756,739 Stats: 19 GS, 6.34 ERA, 1.56 WHIP, 31 BB, 61 K, 98.0 IP WAR: -1.6

Zac Gallen was the bona fide ace of the D-backs rotation during a five-year stretch that saw him finish in the top 10 in NL Cy Young voting three different times, but he fell flat in his contract year in 2025.

After a long stay in free agency following a qualifying offer he turned down, he found his way back to the D-backs on a one-year deal in February looking to rebuild his stock. That hasn't happened, and he struggled to a 13.9 percent strikeout rate before landing on the IL with elbow inflammation in July.

1B Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Toronto Blue Jays

2026 Salary: $35,714,286 Stats: 115 G, 91 OPS+, .263/.337/.356, 26 XBH (7 HR), 46 RBI WAR: 0.9

Vladimir Guerrero Jr. had eight home runs in 18 games during the postseason last year to help the Blue Jays reach the World Series, but he has hit just seven long balls in 486 plate appearances this year, including none at home in Toronto.

The Blue Jays made him the face of the franchise with a 14-year, $500 million extension that kicked in this year, and while he was named an All-Star for the sixth year in a row, his .356 slugging percentage has been one of baseball's most disappointing stats.

2026 Salary: $20,000,000 Stats: 22 GS, 5.11 ERA, 1.48 WHIP, 53 BB, 82 K, 125.0 IP WAR: -0.1

Among the 101 pitchers with at least 100 innings pitched this season, Merrill Kelly ranks 92nd in ERA (5.11) and 98th in FIP (5.72), and he has managed just seven quality starts.

He has surrendered a .314 average and 11 home runs with his fastball, and he has simply not missed as many bats this year. After signing a two-year, $40 million deal during the offseason, the question now is whether he can make good on the second season of that contract.

2026 Salary: $21,225,000 Stats: 7 GS, 5.81 ERA, 1.58 WHIP, 14 BB, 33 K, 31.0 IP WAR: 0.0

Yusei Kikuchi was an All-Star in his first season with the Angels last year, posting a 3.99 ERA with 174 strikeouts in 178.1 innings to kick off a three-year, $63 million deal.

His rocky start this year was backed by a 3.66 FIP and solid 23.2 percent strikeout rate, but he has been sidelined since April 29 with shoulder inflammation. The 35-year-old is currently on a rehab assignment and expected to rejoin the MLB rotation this coming weekend.

2026 Salary: $20,000,000 Stats: 31 G, -32 OPS+, .066/.165/.066, 0 XBH, 4 RBI WAR: -1.0

The Braves saw enough from Ha-Seong Kim in a 24-game audition down the stretch in 2025 to bring him back on a one-year, $20 million deal to serve as the team's primary shortstop.

He tore a tendon in his finger slipping on ice back in South Korea in January, missing the first 41 games of the season. He then missed more than a month with inflammation in the same finger.

Since returning, he is 5-for-76 with zero extra-base hits, and the Braves have been left relying on Mauricio Dubón and Jim Jarvis at shortstop.

2026 Salary: $20,000,000 Stats: 37 G, 21 OPS+, .148/.201/.230, 7 XBH (2 HR), 6 RBI WAR: -1.4

The Mets paid handsomely for a career-high 133 OPS+ and 26 home runs from Jorge Polanco last season, signing him with the intention of making him the team's primary first baseman after Pete Alonso departed in free agency.

Injuries have limited him to 37 games in the first season of a two-year, $40 million deal, and his production has been non-existent when he has been on the field. His hard-hit rate has cratered from 45.8 to 31.0 percent, and his batted-ball metrics across the board are among the worst in baseball.

2026 Salary: $17,500,000 Stats: 91 G, 64 OPS+, .158/.268/.300, 21 XBH (13 HR), 44 RBI WAR: -0.4

Cal Raleigh has the lowest salary of any player on this list, but his fall-off after a record-setting 2025 season has been so drastic that he has earned a spot based purely on production relative to that $17.5 million figure.

Following a 60-homer campaign, he has slugged just 13 long balls in 91 games while his batting average has plummeted 89 points and his strikeout rate has skyrocketed from 26.7 to 32.0 percent. Solid defense behind the dish is the only thing keeping his WAR total out of disaster territory.

2026 Salary: $35,571,429 Stats: Injured, has not played WAR: N/A

That's the last time Anthony Rendon took the field in an MLB game, and after restructuring his contract during the offseason to defer his remaining money, he has spent the final season of his seven-year, $245 million deal at home.

That massive contract will conclude with him logging just 3.8 WAR in 257 games for the Angels, and will go down as one of the worst signings in baseball history.

Stats: 47 G, 77 OPS+, .214/.287/.346, 9 XBH (6 HR), 18 RBI

After whiffing on Kyle Tucker in free agency, the Mets pivoted to trading for Luis Robert Jr. to fill their void in center field, which might end up being a blessing in disguise despite the former White Sox star's struggles this year.

The buy-low move has not paid dividends, but the Mets can end their financial commitment after 2026 by declining a $20 million club option for 2027 and paying a $2 million buyout.

2026 Salary: $32,500,000 Stats: 65 G, 101 OPS+, .203/.307/.390, 20 XBH (12 HR), 30 RBI WAR: 1.4

Despite piling up 18.5 WAR and logging a 158 OPS+ over the last three seasons, Corey Seager averaged just 115 games during that stretch, and his injury issues have been even more pronounced this year.

The 32-year-old has made three separate trips to the injured list this season, dealing with a nagging back issue and a concussion. As one of the highest-paid players on the roster and arguably best player on the team when healthy, his absence has been felt in a major way.

2026 Salary: $24,000,000 Stats: 106 G, 73 OPS+, .210/.269/.354, 25 XBH (14 HR), 41 RBI WAR: -0.5

The surprising Marcus Semien-for-Brandon Nimmo swap in November has a clear winner so far as 2026 winds to a close:

Semien: 106 G, 73 OPS+, -0.5 WAR Nimmo: 119 G, 122 OPS+, 2.0 WAR

Aside from his career-worst offensive production, Semien has also struggled defensively ( -5 DRS, -5 OAA ), which had consistently helped elevate his value floor in years past as a two-time Gold Glove winner.

2026 Salary: $23,333,333 Stats: 12 GS, 4.16 ERA, 1.47 WHIP, 31 BB, 65 K, 62.2 IP WAR: 0.9

On the surface, a 4.16 ERA and 65 strikeouts in 62.2 innings is solid production, even if the peripheral numbers don't paint the most promising picture of sustainability.

However, in the case of Luis Severino, he is the highest-paid player on the Athletics roster by a significant margin. A right shoulder strain likely ended his season in May, and he has not been the rotation anchor the team was hoping for when he was given a three-year, $67 million deal.

2026 Salary: $25,000,000 Stats: 94 G, 89 OPS+, .228/.309/.382, 28 XBH (12 HR), 37 RBI WAR: 0.0

Playing out the final season of a six-year, $150 million deal with the Blue Jays, George Springer has provided mixed results during his time in Toronto.

He was an All-Star in 2022 and a Silver Slugger winner in a 4.8-WAR campaign last year, but he also had multiple down years.

The 36-year-old's time with the team is ending on a low note, as his 89 OPS+ represents a career low and he is on track to play his fewest games since the 2021 season.

2026 Salary: $22,000,000 Stats: 24 G, 100 OPS+, .256/.302/.422, 9 XBH (3 HR), 14 RBI WAR: 0.1

With a 156 OPS+ and 24 home runs in 77 games last season, Giancarlo Stanton showed he can make an impact even while navigating an injury-shortened season, and his .926 OPS and 18 home runs in 48 career playoff games still loom large.

However, he has not played since April 24 after suffering a calf strain and then a setback in his recovery in June. He has resumed running and taking batting practice as he looks to return for the stretch run, but thus far he has done little to earn his salary.

2026 Salary: $23,333,333 Stats: 41 G, 54 OPS+, .206/.244/.303, 10 XBH (3 HR), 19 RBI WAR: -0.1

After playing 163 games during his first three years in Boston, Trevor Story put together a shocking bounce-back season last year when he had a 25-homer, 31-steal, 4.1-WAR season and played 157 games.

That performance made him a candidate to opt-out of the final two years and $55 million of his contract, but he chose to return. A sports hernia has kept him sidelined since May, but before hitting the injured list his 32.4 percent strikeout rate and .206 average made him a non-factor.

Stats: 118 G, 93 OPS+, .230/.326/.366, 32 XBH (11 HR), 54 RBI

In the five seasons prior to reaching free agency for the first time this past winter, Kyle Tucker racked up 25.4 WAR with four All-Star selections, two Silver Sluggers, one Gold Glove and three 20/20 campaigns among his accolades.

That production coupled with the fact that he was still shy of his 30th birthday made him the top free agent on the market, and the Dodgers signed him to a four-year, $240 million contract.

With a 93 OPS+ and 0.1 WAR in 118 games, he has been a replacement-level player despite carrying one of the league's largest payroll figures.

Stats: 9 GS, 2.98 ERA, 0.84 WHIP, 10 BB, 47 K, 45.1 IP

When Brandon Woodruff made the surprise decision to accept his qualifying offer from the Brewers, it changed the math of their offseason, and that unexpected payroll commitment for a club that operates with a small-market budget is a big part of the conversation here.

The 33-year-old was excellent over nine starts before arm fatigue preceded a season-ending shoulder injury.

The Brewers have been one of the best teams in baseball, but Woodruff has not delivered relative to the significant slice of the payroll pie he is occupying.

2026 Salary: $23,370,000 Stats: 86 G, 85 OPS+, .226/.307/.364, 28 XBH (8 HR), 40 RBI WAR: -0.3

While he has not come close to replicating his MVP-level production in the years since his dynamic peak during the 2018 and 2019 seasons, Christian Yelich returned to being a productive player after a few lean years.

He had a 120 OPS+ with 29 home runs and 103 RBI last season while playing in 150 games, but his production has cratered this year to a career-low 85 OPS+ in 86 games. With two seasons to go on his nine-year, $215 million contract, the Brewers will hope for some level of bounce-back down the stretch.

Edwin Díaz was utterly dominant last season for the Mets, posting a 1.63 ERA and 13.3 K/9 with 28 saves in 62 appearances before opting out of his contract and inking a new three-year, $69 million deal with the Dodgers.

After struggling to a 10.50 ERA over his first seven appearances with reduced fastball velocity, he was sidelined with arm fatigue and underwent arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies. He returned on July 29, but has three blown saves in six chances since returning.

Zac Gallen was the bona fide ace of the D-backs rotation during a five-year stretch that saw him finish in the top 10 in NL Cy Young voting three different times, but he fell flat in his contract year in 2025.

After a long stay in free agency following a qualifying offer he turned down, he found his way back to the D-backs on a one-year deal in February looking to rebuild his stock. That hasn't happened, and he struggled to a 13.9 percent strikeout rate before landing on the IL with elbow inflammation in July.
1B Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Toronto Blue Jays

Vladimir Guerrero Jr. had eight home runs in 18 games during the postseason last year to help the Blue Jays reach the World Series, but he has hit just seven long balls in 486 plate appearances this year, including none at home in Toronto.

The Blue Jays made him the face of the franchise with a 14-year, $500 million extension that kicked in this year, and while he was named an All-Star for the sixth year in a row, his .356 slugging percentage has been one of baseball's most disappointing stats.
Among the 101 pitchers with at least 100 innings pitched this season, Merrill Kelly ranks 92nd in ERA (5.11) and 98th in FIP (5.72), and he has managed just seven quality starts.

He has surrendered a .314 average and 11 home runs with his fastball, and he has simply not missed as many bats this year. After signing a two-year, $40 million deal during the offseason, the question now is whether he can make good on the second season of that contract.
Yusei Kikuchi was an All-Star in his first season with the Angels last year, posting a 3.99 ERA with 174 strikeouts in 178.1 innings to kick off a three-year, $63 million deal.

His rocky start this year was backed by a 3.66 FIP and solid 23.2 percent strikeout rate, but he has been sidelined since April 29 with shoulder inflammation. The 35-year-old is currently on a rehab assignment and expected to rejoin the MLB rotation this coming weekend.
The Braves saw enough from Ha-Seong Kim in a 24-game audition down the stretch in 2025 to bring him back on a one-year, $20 million deal to serve as the team's primary shortstop.
He tore a tendon in his finger slipping on ice back in South Korea in January, missing the first 41 games of the season. He then missed more than a month with inflammation in the same finger.
Since returning, he is 5-for-76 with zero extra-base hits, and the Braves have been left relying on Mauricio Dubón and Jim Jarvis at shortstop.

The Mets paid handsomely for a career-high 133 OPS+ and 26 home runs from Jorge Polanco last season, signing him with the intention of making him the team's primary first baseman after Pete Alonso departed in free agency.

Injuries have limited him to 37 games in the first season of a two-year, $40 million deal, and his production has been non-existent when he has been on the field. His hard-hit rate has cratered from 45.8 to 31.0 percent, and his batted-ball metrics across the board are among the worst in baseball.

Cal Raleigh has the lowest salary of any player on this list, but his fall-off after a record-setting 2025 season has been so drastic that he has earned a spot based purely on production relative to that $17.5 million figure.

Following a 60-homer campaign, he has slugged just 13 long balls in 91 games while his batting average has plummeted 89 points and his strikeout rate has skyrocketed from 26.7 to 32.0 percent. Solid defense behind the dish is the only thing keeping his WAR total out of disaster territory.
2026 Salary: $35,571,429 Stats: Injured, has not played WAR: N/A

That's the last time Anthony Rendon took the field in an MLB game, and after restructuring his contract during the offseason to defer his remaining money, he has spent the final season of his seven-year, $245 million deal at home.
That massive contract will conclude with him logging just 3.8 WAR in 257 games for the Angels, and will go down as one of the worst signings in baseball history.

After whiffing on Kyle Tucker in free agency, the Mets pivoted to trading for Luis Robert Jr. to fill their void in center field, which might end up being a blessing in disguise despite the former White Sox star's struggles this year.
The buy-low move has not paid dividends, but the Mets can end their financial commitment after 2026 by declining a $20 million club option for 2027 and paying a $2 million buyout.

Despite piling up 18.5 WAR and logging a 158 OPS+ over the last three seasons, Corey Seager averaged just 115 games during that stretch, and his injury issues have been even more pronounced this year.

The 32-year-old has made three separate trips to the injured list this season, dealing with a nagging back issue and a concussion. As one of the highest-paid players on the roster and arguably best player on the team when healthy, his absence has been felt in a major way.
The surprising Marcus Semien-for-Brandon Nimmo swap in November has a clear winner so far as 2026 winds to a close:
Semien: 106 G, 73 OPS+, -0.5 WAR Nimmo: 119 G, 122 OPS+, 2.0 WAR

Aside from his career-worst offensive production, Semien has also struggled defensively ( -5 DRS, -5 OAA ), which had consistently helped elevate his value floor in years past as a two-time Gold Glove winner.
On the surface, a 4.16 ERA and 65 strikeouts in 62.2 innings is solid production, even if the peripheral numbers don't paint the most promising picture of sustainability.

However, in the case of Luis Severino, he is the highest-paid player on the Athletics roster by a significant margin. A right shoulder strain likely ended his season in May, and he has not been the rotation anchor the team was hoping for when he was given a three-year, $67 million deal.
Playing out the final season of a six-year, $150 million deal with the Blue Jays, George Springer has provided mixed results during his time in Toronto.
He was an All-Star in 2022 and a Silver Slugger winner in a 4.8-WAR campaign last year, but he also had multiple down years.
The 36-year-old's time with the team is ending on a low note, as his 89 OPS+ represents a career low and he is on track to play his fewest games since the 2021 season.

With a 156 OPS+ and 24 home runs in 77 games last season, Giancarlo Stanton showed he can make an impact even while navigating an injury-shortened season, and his .926 OPS and 18 home runs in 48 career playoff games still loom large.

However, he has not played since April 24 after suffering a calf strain and then a setback in his recovery in June. He has resumed running and taking batting practice as he looks to return for the stretch run, but thus far he has done little to earn his salary.

After playing 163 games during his first three years in Boston, Trevor Story put together a shocking bounce-back season last year when he had a 25-homer, 31-steal, 4.1-WAR season and played 157 games.

That performance made him a candidate to opt-out of the final two years and $55 million of his contract, but he chose to return. A sports hernia has kept him sidelined since May, but before hitting the injured list his 32.4 percent strikeout rate and .206 average made him a non-factor.

In the five seasons prior to reaching free agency for the first time this past winter, Kyle Tucker racked up 25.4 WAR with four All-Star selections, two Silver Sluggers, one Gold Glove and three 20/20 campaigns among his accolades.
That production coupled with the fact that he was still shy of his 30th birthday made him the top free agent on the market, and the Dodgers signed him to a four-year, $240 million contract.
With a 93 OPS+ and 0.1 WAR in 118 games, he has been a replacement-level player despite carrying one of the league's largest payroll figures.
Stats: 9 GS, 2.98 ERA, 0.84 WHIP, 10 BB, 47 K, 45.1 IP

When Brandon Woodruff made the surprise decision to accept his qualifying offer from the Brewers, it changed the math of their offseason, and that unexpected payroll commitment for a club that operates with a small-market budget is a big part of the conversation here.
The 33-year-old was excellent over nine starts before arm fatigue preceded a season-ending shoulder injury.
The Brewers have been one of the best teams in baseball, but Woodruff has not delivered relative to the significant slice of the payroll pie he is occupying.

While he has not come close to replicating his MVP-level production in the years since his dynamic peak during the 2018 and 2019 seasons, Christian Yelich returned to being a productive player after a few lean years.

He had a 120 OPS+ with 29 home runs and 103 RBI last season while playing in 150 games, but his production has cratered this year to a career-low 85 OPS+ in 86 games. With two seasons to go on his nine-year, $215 million contract, the Brewers will hope for some level of bounce-back down the stretch.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani vs. Pete Crow-Armstrong NL MVP Race Voted on by MLB Players in ESPN Poll
articles.summary: After winning unanimous NL MVP awards in his first two seasons with the Los Angeles Dodgers, Shohei Ohtani has work to do if he wants to make it three straight based on the results of a player vote.
articles.body:
After winning unanimous NL MVP awards in his first two seasons with the Los Angeles Dodgers, Shohei Ohtani has work to do if he wants to make it three straight based on the results of a player vote.

In a survey of 21 players conducted by ESPN's Jesse Rogers , Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong has a comfortable 15-4 lead over Ohtani as the preferred choice for NL MVP.

Two respondents chose to split the award between the two of them.

This is the first time in years that Ohtani isn't head and shoulders the favorite to win the award. He has been named MVP in three consecutive seasons dating back to his final year with the Los Angeles Angels in 2023.

Since the 2021 season, Ohtani has won four MVP awards in five years. The lone outlier was 2022 when Aaron Judge set a new AL record with 62 home runs, even though Ohtani hit 34 homers and had a 2.33 ERA in 166 innings.

The main reason there is a race between Ohtani and Crow-Armstrong right now is because the Dodgers superstar hasn't been able to pitch for more than a month. His last outing on the mound came on July 3.

Even though Ohtani remains arguably the most dominant hitter in MLB, being limited to DH does hinder his value. However, he still has the benefit of 85.2 innings and a 1.79 ERA to help his case even if he doesn't pitch in a game again.

There does seem to be an out of sight, out of mind feeling because Ohtani hasn't pitched in so long based on comments from the players who voted for Crow-Armstrong.

"One plays elite defense," Athletics pitcher Mark Leiter Jr. told Rogers. "The other doesn't play the field. If you take Ohtani out of the rotation, they don't miss a beat. And if you take him out of the lineup, I still don't think they miss a beat."

Cleveland Guardians first baseman Rhys Hoskins also brought up Ohtani not pitching as a reason for the Cubs star:

"In the true sense of the word, the guy that plays every day probably makes more of an impact on the team every single day. That's how I would weigh it. If Ohtani is pitching, there's not much room. That's the reality. Anyone that's watched PCA or the Cubs over the last two months, this guy is the best player on the field every time he's on the field."

There were several players who responded to Rogers and opted to wait for the rest of the season to play out before making a pick.

Cincinnati Reds pitcher Emilio Pagan brought up the 2022 AL MVP race between Ohtani and Judge as a comparison point:

"I had a debate like this with Rocco Baldelli when I was with Minnesota. It was Ohtani and Judge and at the time. Judge was like the best defensive right fielder in the game. Rocco said you have to take the defensive WAR that Judge provides and compare that to the pitching WAR that Ohtani provides. And then if the offense is even, that's how you can do it. So I'd go PCA. If Ohtani starts pitching again and goes 5-7 innings a start down the stretch, the conversation looks different. If he doesn't pitch again in a real starter's role, then I'd vote for PCA still."

Crow-Armstrong doesn't have the two-way narrative, but he does get a boost from becoming an elite offensive player this season while maintaining his status as arguably the best defensive centerfielder in MLB.

Using advanced metrics including FanGraphs' defensive value, fielding run value and outs above average, Crow-Armstrong ranks first across the board at one of the most important positions on the field.

Combine that with Crow-Armstrong hitting .281/.379/.550 with 30 home runs and 31 stolen bases for a Cubs team that is a safe bet to make the playoffs with a five game lead over the Philadelphia Phillies for the No. 1 wild card spot in the NL, it's easy to make a narrative case for him.

Last year's AL MVP vote between Judge and Cal Raleigh was separated by four first-place votes and 20 total points.

There have been 14 MVP votes in MLB history decided by 10 points or fewer, with the most recent coming in 2017 when Giancarlo Stanton beat Joey Votto by two points.

With just over one month remaining in the 2026 regular season, Ohtani and Crow-Armstrong look like they are running neck and neck for the NL MVP award.

articles.title: Tennis Star Daniil Medvedev Explains Reds Fandom, Drops Surprising Knowledge of MLB Team in Video
articles.summary: Russian tennis star Daniil Medvedev has proved himself to be a true fan of the Cincinnati Reds.
articles.body:
Russian tennis star Daniil Medvedev has proved himself to be a true fan of the Cincinnati Reds.

When quizzed on his Reds fandom after throwing out the first pitch at Monday's game against the St. Louis Cardinals, Medvedev correctly the team's record as well as their leaders in home runs, batting average and wins.

He also came close to guessing Elly De La Cruz's batting average and Chase Burns' ERA.

Medvedev, who was born in Moscow and lives in Monaco, recently told the Cincinnati Enquirer 's Shelby Dermer he decided to become a Reds fan after attending his first baseball game in Ohio following his loss at the 2025 Cincinnati Open.

"I was like, 'why haven't I gone before?'" Medvedev told Dermer. "I started watching baseball more than any other sport, except tennis. Since they were the first team I saw live, why not be a Cincinnati Reds fan?"

Medvedev also told Dermer he now knows "pretty much every player and every stat" regarding the Reds.

"When I'm a fan of something, I like to really be into it. That's my team," Medvedev told Dermer.

Medvedev, ranked as the world's No. 7 player by ATP, was again in town for the Cincinnati Open but did not get to see much more tennis action after throwing out Monday's first pitch.

He was eliminated Tuesday from the third round of the 2026 tournament after a 6-7, 7-6, 6-1 loss to American wild card Brandon Nakashima.

articles.title: Fernando Tatis Jr.'s HR Robbery vs. Mets Captured in Epic New Photo from Padres Win
articles.summary: San Diego Padres star right fielder Fernando Tatis Jr. had one of the most epic performances of the season in Tuesday night's 5-2 win over the New York Mets.
articles.body:
San Diego Padres star right fielder Fernando Tatis Jr. had one of the most epic performances of the season in Tuesday night's 5-2 win over the New York Mets.

In addition to hitting two home runs and driving in three of the Padres' five runs, Tatis helped preserve the victory when he robbed Mets star shortstop Francisco Lindor of a grand slam in the second inning. After soaring over the wall to make the improbable catch, Tatis played it cool and nonchalantly flipped the ball into his hand:

Thanks to Tatis' heroics, the Padres (68-59) have now won eight of their last 10 games and are clinging to a two-game lead for the final wild-card spot in the National League entering Wednesday's series finale against the Mets (57-70).

articles.title: Former Yankees Pitcher Lands Phillies Contract, New MLB Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: Left-hander Nestor Cortes is reportedly making his return from arm surgery with the Philadelphia Phillies, according to FanSided's Robert Murray and the New York Post's Jon Heyman.
articles.body:
Left-hander Nestor Cortes is reportedly making his return from arm surgery with the Philadelphia Phillies, according to FanSided's Robert Murray and the New York Post 's Jon Heyman .

MassLive's Chris Cotillo first reported the sides were in talks.

Cortes played from 2021 to 2024 for the New York Yankees.

He split last season between the Milwaukee Brewers and San Diego Padres before undergoing left arm surgery with a nine to 10 month return timetable last October, per Francys Romero .

Cortes was one of the best left-handers in baseball during his first two seasons as a starter for the Yankees, posting a 2.61 ERA over 50 appearances from 2021 to 2022.

His Yankees career ended with him allowing a walk-off grand slam from the Los Angeles Dodgers' Freddie Freeman in the opening game of the 2024 World Series.

He struggled in his first season away from the Bronx, registering a 6.29 ERA for the Brewers and Padres before undergoing surgery that Romero reported was designed "to repair a small tendon tear in his left arm."

Cortes, who was playing on an expiring deal at the time, hit unrestricted free agency while recovering over the offseason.

He shared a video to social media Wednesday of himself throwing off the mound.

The Athletic's Matt Gelb and Charlotte Varnes reported ahead of the Aug. 3 trade deadline the Phillies were prioritizing the acquisition of a starting pitcher.

The Phillies didn't end up targeting the position before the trade window closed, although Varnes later reported the club sought a starter "in the hours leading up to the deadline."

Philadelphia's rotation is currently led by Zack Wheeler, Cristopher Sánchez and Jesús Luzardo in front of Aaron Nola and Andrew Painter.

Cortes could provide the Phillies with some additional bullpen depth should the club decide to use him in relief as he continues his rehab process.

Should he progress back to his former role as a starter by the end of the season, Cortes could potentially challenge Painter for his spot in the rotation or join in as a sixth man as the Phillies make a push for the postseason.

articles.title: Steve Cohen 'Committed' to Mets President David Stearns, 'He Learns From Mistakes'
articles.summary: New York Mets owner Steve Cohen threw his support behind president of baseball operations David Stearns despite the team falling well short of expectations in 2026.
articles.body:
New York Mets owner Steve Cohen threw his support behind president of baseball operations David Stearns despite the team falling well short of expectations in 2026.

"I thought we had a great trade deadline," Cohen told reporters Wednesday, adding that he's "committed" to Stearns. "David is smart. He knows what he's doing. He's very adaptable. He learns from mistakes. That's what I want in a leader."

Sometimes, a good process can yield bad results, and a team playing poorly may not be a reflection of management.

In the case of Stearns, however, he deserves his share of blame for the Mets' 57-70 record and last-place standing in the National League East. He made a lot of changes to the roster for one offseason, and almost every one of his notable additions has underwhelmed.

"We might have taken too much risk as far as when you think about all the changes that were made," Cohen said . "Whenever there are significant changes, sometimes it takes a while to integrate. Those are the things I'm looking at. It's an example of where we can be better."

It doesn't help that the Milwaukee Brewers, Stearns' old team, have continued to thrive after he stepped back from an everyday role in 2022 and left altogether following the 2023 season.

The Brewers have won three straight NL Central titles and advanced to the NLCS last year. While Stearns contributed to the structure that made the franchise competitive for nearly a decade, he clearly wasn't the only person responsible for that happening.

Combine that with the mess in Queens and Stearns' reputation is undoubtedly suffering.

The Mets fired manager Carlos Mendoza in June, giving him just two-and-a-half seasons in the role. Cohen doesn't sound willing to wipe the slate totally clean by reshuffling the front office as well.

Stearns will have the opportunity to get New York back on the right course. Whether he can execute a quick turnaround is another question.

articles.title: Paul Skenes' Box-Score Player Stats, Highlights vs. Tigers After Pirates Pushed Start Back
articles.summary: Despite having his start pushed back to give him extra rest, Pittsburgh Pirates star Paul Skenes' first outing in eight days looked like a lot of his recent performances.
articles.body:
Despite having his start pushed back to give him extra rest, Pittsburgh Pirates star Paul Skenes' first outing in eight days looked like a lot of his recent performances.

Skenes threw 81 pitches over 4.1 innings against the Detroit Tigers on Wednesday. He allowed three earned runs on four hits, walked four and struck out five.

One encouraging sign was Skenes' fastball velocity was in line with his season average.

Pirates manager Don Kelly announced Sunday that Skenes' start was being pushed back to give him extra rest, but there was no concern of any injury.

Skenes last pitched on Aug. 11 against the Miami Marlins. His stat line from the game was solid with five hits, two runs allowed (one earned) and four strikeouts in five innings of a 2-0 loss.

The Pirates pulled Skenes after just 65 pitches due in part to a noticeable dip in his velocity. He threw a total of 14 fastballs against the Marlins with just four of them clocked at 96.0 mph or higher.

Just for comparison, Skenes also threw 14 fastballs in his second start of the season against the Cincinnati Reds on April 1. Thirteen of them were at least 96.0 mph and the slowest was at 95.5 mph.

Skenes' average fastball velocity in 2026 is 96.8 mph, down exactly two miles per hour from his rookie year and 1.4 miles per hour from last season.

In addition to the dip in velocity, Skenes' command has not been sharp. Wednesday marked his third game of the season allowing four walks and 13th time issuing at least two free passes in 26 starts.

Skenes had a total of five games in the previous two years combined (55 starts) in which he issued at least four walks.

The three-time All-Star's ERA this season now sits at 3.95 after Wednesday's outing, more than double his 1.97 mark from his 2025 Cy Young campaign.
paragraphs: Despite having his start pushed back to give him extra rest, Pittsburgh Pirates star Paul Skenes' first outing in eight days looked like a lot of his recent performances.
Skenes threw 81 pitches over 4.1 innings against the Detroit Tigers on Wednesday. He allowed three earned runs on four hits, walked four and struck out five.
One encouraging sign was Skenes' fastball velocity was in line with his season average.
Pirates manager Don Kelly announced Sunday that Skenes' start was being pushed back to give him extra rest, but there was no concern of any injury.
Skenes last pitched on Aug. 11 against the Miami Marlins. His stat line from the game was solid with five hits, two runs allowed (one earned) and four strikeouts in five innings of a 2-0 loss.

The Pirates pulled Skenes after just 65 pitches due in part to a noticeable dip in his velocity. He threw a total of 14 fastballs against the Marlins with just four of them clocked at 96.0 mph or higher.
Just for comparison, Skenes also threw 14 fastballs in his second start of the season against the Cincinnati Reds on April 1. Thirteen of them were at least 96.0 mph and the slowest was at 95.5 mph.
Skenes' average fastball velocity in 2026 is 96.8 mph, down exactly two miles per hour from his rookie year and 1.4 miles per hour from last season.
In addition to the dip in velocity, Skenes' command has not been sharp. Wednesday marked his third game of the season allowing four walks and 13th time issuing at least two free passes in 26 starts.
Skenes had a total of five games in the previous two years combined (55 starts) in which he issued at least four walks.
The three-time All-Star's ERA this season now sits at 3.95 after Wednesday's outing, more than double his 1.97 mark from his 2025 Cy Young campaign.

articles.title: Little League World Series 2026 Wednesday Scores, Bracket Results and Highlights
articles.summary: A summer institution is now upon us.
articles.body:
The Little League World Series kicked off play Wednesday in Williamsport, Pennsylvania, with four games spread across the day.

The action is split equally between the United States and international brackets. Here's what unfolded to get the tournament underway.

Little League World Series 2026 Monday Schedule, TV Info and Bracket Predictions

Latin America (Nicaragua) 2, Caribbean (Dominican Republic) 1

Northwest (Tacoma, Wash.) 2 vs. Southeast (Phenix City, Ala.) 0

Asia-Pacific (South Korea) 7, Canada (Vancouver, British Columbia) 0

Metro (Bayonne, N.J.) 2, New England (Bridgewater, Mass.) 1

The squad from Leon, Nicaragua, held on to beat the Caribbean champions 2-1 in Wednesday's first contest.

A two-out double from Clemente Sevilla Pichardo put Nicaragua ahead in the first inning. Moisés Estrada Juaréz scored from second after having advanced on a wild pitch.

Christofer Pichardo got two quick outs for the Dominican Republic to start the second inning, only to load the bases thanks to a single and two walks. A free pass to Sergio Jirón Fuentes brought brought home Nicaragua's second run.

The Dominican Republic halved the deficit with an RBI double by Ethan Estevez in the fifth but couldn't add onto that.

Sevilla Pichardo weaved a gem on the mound, going 5.2 innings and striking out 12 batters. Estrada Juaréz got the final out but not without some drama.

With a runner on second, Yansel Guzman singled to right field. James Cruceta Nin tried to score and was out by some distance after Sevilla Pichardo unleashed a frozen rope from right.

The southpaw certainly had a game to remember.

Extra innings were needed to separate the Northwest and Southeast teams, and Washington came out on top 2-0.

Kasen Workman singled to right with two outs in the top of the seventh. The runner from third scored, and an error by right fielder Lorenzo Quintero allowed the runner on second to reach home as well.

Once it had a turn to bat, Alabama was unable to move the runner over from second. Jerry Taylor, Easton Allen and Kinley Rasmus went down in order to end the game.

Frankie McCabe and Winston Weaver combined to surrender just one hit to Alabama. McCabe started and went five innings, with Weaver going the final two.

On the other side, Rasmus was equally as dominant. Across six innings of work, she allowed one hit and struck out eight, tying Mo'ne Davis' strikeout record for a girl's player in the LLBWS.

Based on the first two games, offense might be at a premium in this year's Little League World Series.

The group from Seoul, South Korea, had little trouble dispatching of the Canadian representative, winning its first game 7-0.

South Korea took the lead in the second inning on an RBI single by Ji Hoo Lee. Ji Hwan Hong hammered a solo home run to left to double the advantage in the third.

Later in the inning, two more runs came in courtesy of a double by Jae Hyun Maeng.

South Korea manufactured more offense in the fourth, scoring on a fielder's choice and then a sacrifice fly. An error by Canada shortstop Cruz Krpan brought in the game's final run.

Needing to mount a massive comeback in the final inning, Daniel Huang led off the sixth with a single. Ji Hwan Hong proceeded to strike out three straight batters and wrap up the victory.

The Metro representatives from Bayonne, New Jersey picked up a thrilling 2-1 victory over the New England squad from Bridgewater, Massachusetts in the final game of the day.

Bayonne got on the board in the bottom of the first inning, taking an early 1-0 lead after Gabe Garcia Jr. scored on a wild pitch.

Bridgewater eventually responded in the top of the third, as Anthony Sullivan tied the contest with a solo home run to center field.

With the score still tied 1-1 in the sixth inning, Mason Rincon hit a walk-off homer that allowed Bayonne to emerge victorious.

Rincon also pitched 4.1 innings in the win, amassing eight strikeouts compared to three walks while allowing just one earned run.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani's Dodgers Cleats From 2025 Tokyo Series Sell for Record, Joins Jordan, Kobe in History
articles.summary: A pair of Shohei Ohtani's cleats made history on Wednesday.
articles.body:
A pair of Shohei Ohtani's cleats made history on Wednesday.

The New Balance cleats Ohtani wore for the 2025 Tokyo Series sold for $440,055, making a new record for the highest-selling baseball cleat ever. Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant are the only other athletes to have a pair of shoes sell for more than $300,000.

The high price isn't all that surprising given Ohtani's star power. The Los Angeles Dodgers star is one of the most popular athletes of all time, gaining recognition both in the United States and around the world.

The particular cleats that sold this week are extra special since they have his rare Japanese Kanji signature and feature images of his dog, Decoy. He also wore them in his first MLB game in Japan.

Ohtani is well on his way to establishing himself as one of the greatest baseball players ever, so the cleats sold Wednesday should be worth even more in a few years.

articles.title: Kinley Rasmus Ties Mo'ne Davis' LLWS Record for Most Strikeouts By a Girl in 1 Game
articles.summary: Kinley Rasmus had a historic day on the mound on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Kinley Rasmus had a historic day on the mound on Wednesday.

The Phenix City Alabama Little League pitcher recorded eight strikeouts through six innings against Washington, tying Mo'ne Davis for the most strikeouts by a girl pitcher in a Little League World Series game.

Davis was just the fourth American girl to play in the Little League World Series and was the first girl to pitch a winning game in 2014, setting the stage for players like Rasmus to star on youth sports' biggest stage.

But those familiar with Rasmus likely aren't surprised to see her dominate the way she did on Wednesday.

She is the niece of former MLB center fielder Colby Rasmus, who led Phenix City to Williamsport in 1999, the team's last appearance.

He's now an assistant coach for the team, and his brother, Case, is the head coach of the team. Case played four seasons in minor league baseball, and his son is on the team with Kinley.

So the Rasmus family is no stranger to the Little League World Series, and Kinley is looking to lead Phenix City to its first-ever championship.

"I just always hear my dad talking about [Williamsport] and how much fun he had, and I just want to do the same thing," Kinley said, per ESPN's J.J. Post .

Before her outstanding showing on Wednesday, Kinley pitched a complete-game shutout in the regional final and went 6-for-8 with two RBIs and four walks during the tournament.

articles.title: Paul Skenes Talks Struggles, Has to 'Remember What's Real' amid 'Outside' Criticism
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes is trying to tune out the noise as he attempts to shake out of his current funk.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes is trying to tune out the noise as he attempts to shake out of his current funk.

Following Wednesday's 4-3 win over the Detroit Tigers, Skenes told reporters his focus is on emphasizing "what's real and what's not."

"Just objective numbers, watching the game, execution, all that stuff," he said when asked to elaborate on that remark. "Not anything from the outside."

Skenes only lasted 4.1 innings against Detroit. He was charged with three earned runs, having allowed two himself and watching as McGonigle gave the Tigers a 3-1 lead immediately after he exited.

The Pirates eventually came out on top thanks to a pair of solo homers by Rafael Flores Jr. and Brandon Lowe in the bottom of the ninth.

Skenes' forgettable start will only embolden those who believe something is wrong with the right-hander. Maybe his mechanics are off. Perhaps he's working through an injury of some sort.

Whether there's a straightforward explanation or not, giving the three-time All-Star some extra rest didn't help.

Lowe hit on what might actually be happening.

"I think the world's been spoiled on who Paul Skenes really is," he said. "He had probably the best starting stretch to a career ever. And now he's not the greatest pitcher on the face of the planet for a few months, and people were worried and freaking out a bit."

Skenes may also be paying a price for a defense many flagged as a possible problem before Opening Day. Entering Wednesday, his FIP (2.99) was nearly a full run lower than his ERA (3.88), and his batting average on balls in play has gone from .284 and .273 through his first two years to .306, per FanGraphs .

The Pirates are trying to push for a wild-card spot. At 63-66, they're 5.5 games back of the final spot.

For Skenes, it might be a case of keeping his head down and getting to the offseason, when he'll have time to mentally decompress and reset.
