Bagwell played a role in the disastrous signing of José Abreu during the 2023 offseason. Crane helped influence the return of Carlos Correa at the 2025 trade deadline, and Correa's sizable contract is aging worse and worse.

In general, the results from Houston's win-now moves speak for themselves. They have a top-10 payroll and one of MLB's worst farm systems . That's a rough combination for a team that looks so far away from seriously contending.
The obvious concern as it relates to the Astros' GM search is whether Crane is willing to let Brown's replacement execute a long-term plan as they see fit.

articles.title: Rob Manfred Says MLB, MLBPA Meet 'Regularly' for CBA Talks Amid Salary Cap Buzz
articles.summary: MLB commissioner Rob Manfred told ESPN on Sunday that "we're planning on playing baseball next year" amidst mounting pessimism about the ongoing collective bargaining negotiations and the possibility of a lockout in 2027.
articles.body:
MLB commissioner Rob Manfred told ESPN on Sunday that "we're planning on playing baseball next year" amidst mounting pessimism about the ongoing collective bargaining negotiations and the possibility of a lockout in 2027.

"We're meeting regularly, which is good," he added during the Little League Classic regarding those labor talks. "Every week, we've had days where we've met with the players. It's early, but we've got a lot of work to do, and we're at it. Look, our goal is to make a deal. We want to make a deal. We want to play baseball next year. We're planning on playing baseball next year."

The main hurdle in negotiations is the desire from the owners to add a salary cap, something the MLBPA has consistently said it would never accept. The players, meanwhile, are seeking a higher minimum salary, reduced restrictions on the luxury tax threshold and improvements to the bonus pool before arbitration.

Most fans want more competitive balance, annoyed that teams like the Dodgers seem to endlessly add talent and salary while five MLB franchises currently have a payroll less than $100 million. There's a strong argument to be made that more competitive balance could be added by increasing the payroll floor, adding stricter rules regarding deferred contracts and finding unique ways to increase revenue sharing, however.

Players have argued that a salary cap would limit their earning potential in the long term and that the owners are largely seeking a cap to increase franchise valuations . It also would be complicated for teams set to have payrolls above the $245.3 million hard cap in future seasons, or for teams dramatically below the owners' proposed $171.2 million floor. Some sort of grace period, perhaps over multiple seasons, would be necessary.

Either way, the expectation remains that the owners will lock out the players if a salary cap isn't accepted. Regardless of Manfred's remarks, the 2027 season remains very much in jeopardy.

articles.title: Jacob Young Reacts to 'Spider-Man' Wall Catch After Epic HR Robbery Highlight for Nationals
articles.summary: Washington Nationals center fielder Jacob Young made an incredible catch on Sunday, scaling the wall to deny the Miami Marlins' Heriberto Hernández a home run.
articles.body:
Washington Nationals center fielder Jacob Young made an incredible catch on Sunday, scaling the wall to deny the Miami Marlins' Heriberto Hernández a home run.

Young has been given the Spider-Man nickname in the past, and it sure seemed apt after that grab.

"It's a fun one," he told MLB.com's Perla Paredes regarding the nickname. "But you know, if [I] keep catching the ball, [the fans] can call me whatever they want."

As for scaling the wall to make the grab, Young called it "instinctual" and said that his mindset is to just "go try to catch everything."

"It just kind of ended up in the spot where I like to climb them," he added. "And I'm gonna give myself a chance. And when I looked up, the ball was there, so it was cool to be able to get [Jackson] a couple more innings and keep us in the game."

The Nationals ultimately lost 6-2 anyway, but at least Young provided one of the season's best highlights.

articles.title: Little League World Series 2026 Monday Scores, Bracket Results and Highlights
articles.summary: Eight teams found themselves facing elimination at the Little League World Series in Williamsport on Monday, with only four teams set to advance on the bottom half of the bracket.
articles.body:
Eight teams found themselves facing elimination at the Little League World Series in Williamsport on Monday, with only four teams set to advance on the bottom half of the bracket .

Below, we'll break down the day's schedule, scores and top highlights as the Little League World Series continued.

Little League World Series 2026 Monday Schedule, TV Info and Bracket Predictions

It took Canada and Panama into extra innings to score any runs. But boy was the seventh inning wild.

Led by RBI by Connor Matsuda, Connor Ross and Jason Mezzarobba, Canada put up three runs in the top of the seventh and held on for dear life in the bottom half of the frame, winning 3-2.

Panama got two back on Jeickot Sánchez's double and a wild pitch but managed to secure the win. Canadien starter Jacob Massel was masterful, giving up just two hits, three walks and no runs while striking out seven across five innings.

Canada's seventh-inning heroics spoiled an epic performance from Panama starter Obed Fuentes, who struck out 12 batters and didn't give up a hit in six innings.

Up next for Canada is a matchup against Asia-Pacific.

Led by Zach Hilton's two RBI and Walker Osborne's two runs, Great Lakes knocked out Southwest on Monday, 6-1.

Bob Frazier pitched 4.2 scoreless innings for Great Lakes, striking out four. Up next for Great Lakes is a matchup against the representative from Metro.

Yunosuke Yabe's pair of home runs and Takeru Yorozu's solo shot led Japan to a 3-2 victory over Europe-Asia on Monday.

The pair provided double duty on the mound, combining to strike out 13 batters while giving up just five hits and two runs.

Japan will now face Mexico as they look to stay alive in Williamsport.

It took extra-inning drama, but Southeast overcame a 5-0 deficit and defeated Mid-Atlantic 6-5.

Mid-Atlantic looked like it was well on the way to victory when it jumped out to a 5-0 advantage behind a two-run homer from Cole Warner, but Southeast answered with five runs in the third inning.

That set the stage for two-way star Kinley Rasmus—who drove in one of the runs in the fifth—to take the mound. All she did was strike out six in 4.2 shutout innings in relief to keep the game tied into the seventh.

And that is when Brooks Cameron played the role of hero with the game-winning hit in the extra inning.

articles.title: Ketel Marte lost the benefit of the doubt long before he showed up to the casino
articles.summary: Baseball culture values consistency and accountability. The Diamondbacks' star has displayed neither of those things.
articles.body:
There was Ketel Marte , in plain sight, hitting on a green surface.

Wearing a black tee, red shorts and Jordan 4s, the Diamondbacks ' second baseman appeared mighty comfortable at a Talking Stick Casino blackjack table on Friday night . Normally, that wouldn't have ruffled many feathers. Ballplayers are adults, free citizens, allowed to do whatever they please with their free time.

That was true for Marte, currently on the IL due to a knee issue . He'd already completed that day's rehab work at the team's Salt River spring training facility. It's not abnormal for D-backs players to do their rehab work at the Salt River facility. It's also not abnormal for those players to head home afterward, instead of driving to the game at Chase Field. In that respect, Marte's conduct was ordinary.

But given his tumultuous and questionable behavior last week , the photos and videos of Marte wandering around Talking Stick during one of his team's games were an optical dumpster fire.

The entire fiasco began last Monday, when the three-time All-Star didn't show up to Fenway Park for the opening game of the club's series against the Red Sox . He was a late scratch from the lineup due to the unexplained absence. Still in the dark about his status, Arizona put Marte on the restricted list. Communication between player and team was somewhere between truncated and nonexistent . One week later, clarity about specifics remains light. The whole thing has been bizarre, perplexing and concerning for someone who has struggled with mental health in the past .

Last season, Marte was similarly unreachable following the All-Star break. Arizona put him on the restricted list then as well , with a story about a break-in at Marte's Phoenix-area home . The player himself was in the Dominican Republic during that time. He returned to the team in short order and appeared to reintegrate himself well enough , despite reports that some around the Snakes were frustrated with Marte and his willingness to take days off.

That context is important, as it paints a more complete picture of a player who has repeatedly failed to take responsibility for his actions — or, rather, his inaction. As such, Marte has lost both the benefit of the doubt and the respect of many in his clubhouse.

To be clear, while his decision to partake in a few games of chance is a tough look, it did little to worsen a reputation that was already in disarray. Marte's decision to ghost his teammates during a pennant race and his failure to explain his whereabouts were far more damaging than any trip to the casino could be. Baseball culture and its daily grind place a high value on consistency and accountability. Marte, both recently and over the long term, has displayed neither of those things.

If there are significant mental health issues at play in this case, those should be treated with grace. The baseball world and society as a whole have grown more aware and accepting of such situations. That's a good thing. But having a tough time does not excuse someone from conducting themselves with tact and respect.

As things stand, we're left to conclude that Marte is disjointed, dumb or uncaring. Perhaps a combination of those. At the very least, he has struggled to understand that his actions have an impact on the people around him.

On the moral ladder of inexcusability, the crime of not showing up to work and failing to justify that absence is relatively low. Worse people have done far worse things. So too have worse ballplayers. Marte has broken no laws and just one team rule. And because he's one of the most talented hitters on the planet, there is a path to, if not absolution, then at least forgiveness.

But Marte must apologize to his teammates and mean it. He must apologize to his bosses, manager Torey Lovullo and GM Mike Hazen, folks who have repeatedly put their own reputations on the line in support of an individual who has not reciprocated in kind. Marte also owes some sort of apology to the fans, the people who pay his salary, enable his lifestyle and fund his hobbies.

Then, if he comes back and hits once again, all will be forgotten. He just has to be on a baseball field that time.

articles.title: Ketel Marte Return Timeline Updated by D-Backs Manager After Stints on Injured, Restricted Lists
articles.summary: The Arizona Diamondbacks have a plan to get second baseman Ketel Marte back on the field after he was placed on the restricted list and then the injured list in the aftermath of him not showing up for a game against the Boston Red Sox.
articles.body:
The Arizona Diamondbacks have a plan to get second baseman Ketel Marte back on the field after he was placed on the restricted list and then the injured list in the aftermath of him not showing up for a game against the Boston Red Sox.

Arizona manager Torey Lovullo said the team hopes to have Marte back in the lineup for its series against the Philadelphia Phillies starting Aug. 31.

"That's what we're thinking about," Lovullo said, per David Brandt of the Associated Press. "I think that will be the 10th day or the 11th day, so there is definitely a strategy to get him back on the field, get him healthy."

Brandt noted the Diamondbacks put Marte on the restricted list after he didn't show up to Fenway Park but eventually moved him to the 10-day injured list because of mild inflammation in his left knee.

The story was once again in the headlines Friday when Marte was seen in a casino during the Diamondbacks' game against the Cincinnati Reds. Lovullo told reporters at the time he was "free to do whatever he wants" as long as he did his rehab work:

According to Brandt, Marte is yet to address his teammates about his disappearance.

"We're trying to create the softest space for him to re-emerge back in this environment," Lovullo said. "That's up to him however he wants to do it. I cannot force a human being to do something that I want to do, or anybody in this room wants to do, or a fan wants to do.

"One of the things that makes Ketel such an extraordinary player is he goes to the beat of his own drum. I respect that."

Marte has appeared in 118 games this season and is slashing .249/.314/.446 with 21 home runs, 67 RBI and four stolen bases.

The 2023 National League Championship Series MVP was also a back-to-back All-Star and Silver Slugger winner in 2024 and 2025. He is a key part of the lineup for an Arizona team hoping to make a late charge.

The Diamondbacks enter Monday's game against the Chicago Cubs two games behind the San Diego Padres for the final wild-card spot in the National League.

articles.title: Kinley Rasmus' Box Score Stats, Highlights from 1st Game After Tying Mo'ne Davis' LLWS Record
articles.summary: Less than a week after tying Mo'ne Davis' Little League World Series record for strikeouts by a girl, the Phenix City, Alabama pitcher made more history.
articles.body:
Less than a week after tying Mo'ne Davis' Little League World Series record for strikeouts by a girl, the Phenix City, Alabama pitcher made more history.

She brought her strikeout total up to 14 for the tournament, once again tying Davis. In the process, she helped lead Alabama to a 6-5 win in an elimination game against Pennsylvania.

Rasmus came on to the mound in the top of the third with Alabama down five runs and desperate for something to change on defense. The star pitcher gave it exactly what it needed, picking up a double play to end the inning and stop the bleeding.

In the bottom of the third, Alabama cut into the lead with a handful of RBI singles before Rasmus stepped up to the plate and delivered the game-tying RBI on a single to left field.

Rasmus was spectacular on the mound the rest of the way, giving up just two hits over the final four innings.

She finished with six strikeouts and went 1-for-3 at the plate.

Rasmus was the hero on the mound, but Brooks Cameron served as the hero on offense. In extra innings, Alabama had the bases loaded with no outs, and Cameron hit one up the middle of the infield to drive in the game-winning run.

With Rasmus having tied Davis' Little League World Series record for strikeouts in the tournament, she'll have the chance to make even more history the next time up after Alabama punched its ticket to the next round.

articles.title: Cal Raleigh busts out of slump, posts first career 3-homer game to power Mariners past Phillies
articles.summary: Amid a rough 2026 campaign, Raleigh had the biggest night of his career on Monday.
articles.body:
The Seattle Mariners star, after backing up a breakout campaign in 2025 with a very rough go this season, seems to have found his stride again. Raleigh rattled off three home runs to help lift the Mariners to a 9-2 win over the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday night. It was the first three-homer game of his career.

Raleigh opened the night with a two-run shot to right in the first inning at T-Mobile Park, which helped push the Mariners to a 5-1 lead. It was the second home run of the inning for Seattle, too, following Julio Rodríguez 's three-run shot.

Raleigh then followed suit with a deep solo homer in the fifth inning, which extended the Mariners' lead. The first two homers both came off Phillies starter Zack Wheeler .

Cal Raleigh goes deep for the second time in this game 💪 https://t.co/lGEX1Ccf6s pic.twitter.com/YR1srNkvJm — MLB (@MLB) August 25, 2026

Cal Raleigh goes deep for the second time in this game 💪 https://t.co/lGEX1Ccf6s pic.twitter.com/YR1srNkvJm

And finally, Raleigh just barely got his third one over the wall in right field in the seventh inning for good measure. All three of his homers were on nearly identical trajectories.

BIG DUMPER FOR A THIRD TIME 😱 Cal Raleigh has the first 3-homer game of his career! pic.twitter.com/sK00IQgiin — MLB (@MLB) August 25, 2026

BIG DUMPER FOR A THIRD TIME 😱 Cal Raleigh has the first 3-homer game of his career! pic.twitter.com/sK00IQgiin

Raleigh entered Monday night with just a .159 batting average with 47 RBI and only 14 home runs. It was only two weeks ago that Raleigh — who drilled 60 home runs, made his first All-Star team and won the Home Run Derby in 2025 — sounded incredibly down about his play during a losing skid .

"It's not good," he said . "We're not playing well. That starts with me. I'm awful. I've got to find a way to be better and to help bring the guys along. We just gotta play better. We're just playing very, very, very bad baseball in every facet of the game. We gotta pick it up — from the energy standpoint to the execution to the little things in the game that help you win baseball games. We're just not doing those things right now."

Blue Jays add SP Shane Bieber to IL, giving Toronto thin pitching depth in AL wild-card race

Ketel Marte lost the benefit of the doubt long before he showed up to the casino

Mariners shortstop Colt Emerson to have season-ending surgery on left wrist

The win marked Seattle's third in its past four outings, though it entered Monday fresh off a 19-2 beatdown by the Chicago Cubs . The win moved the Mariners to 63-69 on the year, three games back of the AL West-leading Texas Rangers and three games back of the AL's final wild-card spot.

With a little more than a month left in the regular season, they are running out of time to make a move.

One game won't break him out of his funk completely, but Monday's outing was a flash of the greatness that Raleigh showed throughout 2025. Whether that's enough to spark a late rally for the Mariners and get a postseason push going, though, remains to be seen.

Mariners shortstop Colt Emerson to have season-ending surgery on left wrist

The win marked Seattle's third in its past four outings, though it entered Monday fresh off a 19-2 beatdown by the Chicago Cubs . The win moved the Mariners to 63-69 on the year, three games back of the AL West-leading Texas Rangers and three games back of the AL's final wild-card spot.
With a little more than a month left in the regular season, they are running out of time to make a move.

One game won't break him out of his funk completely, but Monday's outing was a flash of the greatness that Raleigh showed throughout 2025. Whether that's enough to spark a late rally for the Mariners and get a postseason push going, though, remains to be seen.

articles.title: 15 Yankees Options to Replace Giancarlo Stanton and Find Aaron Judge's Next Co-Star in 2027
articles.summary: It isn't too soon to wonder if we've seen the last of Giancarlo Stanton as a New York Yankee. If we have, the search for his replacement must start now.
articles.body:
It isn't too soon to wonder if we've seen the last of Giancarlo Stanton as a New York Yankee. If we have, the search for his replacement must start now.

Coming into this year, Stanton was a 36-year-old DH with a lengthy injury history. He has since added to it, originally going on the IL with a right calf strain in April and then straining his left calf while trying to run as part of his recovery program. His season, at least, is likely over.

Stanton has missed almost as many games (694) as he's played in (764) since he joined the Yankees in 2018. He has one guaranteed year left on his contract at $25 million, followed by a $10 million buyout on a $25 million club option for 2028.

When B/R ran a poll on what the Yankees should do with Stanton, only 11 percent of respondents were in favor of keeping the 2017 NL MVP. Most preferred him getting released or retiring—the latter would surely require a buyout.

It'll come down to what Stanton wants. If he wants a shot at the 44 home runs he needs to get to 500, he could be granted his release. If he's tired of all the injuries, retirement and the buyout are his best options.

Either way, the Yankees only need to look back to Stanton's 2024 postseason for evidence that even Aaron Judge needs a Robin to his Batman. While they could trust Cody Bellinger , Ben Rice , Luis García Jr. or Spencer Jones to fill that role, they're better off eyeing potential solutions on the free-agent and trade markets.

5 Options for the Yankees in Free Agency

The Pie in the Sky: DH/RHP Shohei Ohtani (LAD)

This is an extreme long shot. Mark Walter has agreed to sell the Los Angeles Lakers, and recent reporting has examined whether that development could affect the Dodgers' ownership outlook.

There is no indication the Dodgers are currently for sale; in fact, The Athletic reported that the signs point against a sale for now. Still, a sale would carry significant implications for Shohei Ohtani, whose 10-year, $700 million contract reportedly includes an opt-out provision if Walter sells the club.

Per Alden Gonzalez of ESPN, the four-time MVP isn't likely to take advantage of that clause. Even if he did, there's no rule that says the Dodgers' subsequent new owners couldn't bring him back.

Still, if there's a one-in-a-million chance of the Yankees having a shot at Ohtani, neither Heaven nor Earth should stand in their way at acquiring the best player baseball has ever known.

The More Likely Targets: LF Randy Arozarena (SEA), 2B Brandon Lowe (PIT), LF Ian Happ (CHC), RF Seiya Suzuki (CHC)

Ohtani aside, these are the best hitters who are slated to hit free agency this winter. It is indeed that weak of a crop.

All of these players are capable of hitting 25 home runs in a season, and Arozarena can add 20 stolen bases. His role in the recent World Baseball Classic controversy could invite added scrutiny in a market like New York. He will also be 32 by Opening Day 2027.

The lefty-hitting, pull-happy Lowe has the best Yankee Stadium profile on paper, but not so much in practice. He has a .650 OPS there for his career, and that's over an ample sample of 44 games.

The switch-hitting Happ is more of a well-rounded type than a slugger, so Suzuki is the better option if all the Yankees want is an impact bat. He's cleared a .800 OPS four years in a row, and has a high of 32 home runs.

10 Options for the Yankees on the Trade Market

The Best Possible Option: DH/LF Yordan Alvarez (HOU)

There was some Alvarez trade buzz earlier this year, and the Houston Astros just decided to part ways with GM Dana Brown. Given this and the dire state of their farm system , maybe we're in for the Astros making a Mookie Betts-style trade.

Even if it's highly unlikely, the Yankees would need to be at the front of the line. Alvarez is another injury-prone guy, yet he's also a guy with a career 168 OPS+ and AL-best marks for AVG, OBP, SLG, OPS, home runs and RBI this year. He also has a 1.133 OPS at Yankee Stadium.

As for the acquisition cost, "huge" doesn't cover it. Alvarez is 29 and owed a modest $53.7 million across 2027 and 2028.

The Funniest Possible Option: DH/1B Rafael Devers (SFG)

Buster Posey was said to be willing to listen on Devers as far back as June . If so, Devers and his $225 million remaining contract are sure to be on the block this winter.

Given how much of a nemesis Devers was to the Yankees (and to Gerrit Cole , specifically) during his time in Boston, one doubts whether the Yankees will be seriously interested. He's also not a can't-miss star at this point. Devers is still just 29, but rocking a .319 OBP and .788 OPS.

However, a powerful lefty will never not be an appealing target for the Yankees. If we end up seeing Devers in pinstripes hitting homers against the Red Sox in support of Cole, we'll have confirmation that we are living in the most chaotic timeline.

Doesn't Hurt to Ask: CF Mike Trout (LAA), CF Byron Buxton (MIN), 1B Bryce Harper (PHI), 1B Munetaka Murakami (CHW)

The Yankees will have an opening in center field once Trent Grisham files for free agency, so it especially makes sense to inquire on Trout and Buxton. Brian Cashman just shouldn't expect to get anywhere on either. Both are institutions with their respective teams, and neither has ever expressed interest in getting traded.

After what Dave Dombrowski said last year , Harper could be a different story. As a two-time MVP who can play first base and right field and who has a powerful left-handed swing, he's a perfect Yankees target on paper. Yet he also has 10-and-5 rights and can block any trade, meaning he would have to approve any move even if the Philadelphia Phillies are willing to talk.

Murakami is a wild card. He's been a hit in his debut with the Chicago White Sox, cranking 29 homers in 95 games. He's only signed through 2027, though, so you wonder if the Pale Hose could entertain offers on the slugger if potential extension talks go nowhere.

Shoot Your Shot: C Hunter Goodman (COL), SS/2B CJ Abrams (WAS), SS Zach Neto (LAA), 2B Ketel Marte (ARI)

Goodman, Abrams and Neto were popular trade candidates before the trade deadline, and the Yankees were connected to at least two of them.

Because George Lombard Jr. has since taken over at shortstop, neither Abrams nor Neto is as good of a fit these days. Either could still hypothetically provide 20-20 upside at second base or third base, though, so it's best not to take them off the board altogether.

Of all the names discussed, Marte is a potential buyer-beware option for the Yankees. He is a three-time All-Star who could fit as an on-field replacement for Jazz Chisholm Jr. However, his recent absence from the Diamondbacks while receiving injury treatment would likely invite added scrutiny in New York.

As such, Goodman remains the best fit for the Yankees. A catcher who can give you 30-homer seasons is a rare thing, and he isn't even a Coors Field product. This year, he has a .900 OPS and 19 of his 34 homers on the road.

Best guess: He won't be on the Yankees next year, but he won't retire either.

As Chris Kirschner of The Athletic noted, Stanton's remaining salary is "within the range that owner Hal Steinbrenner has been willing to absorb to move on from a player." He could therefore be comfortable with simply releasing Stanton, who would then have his pick of 29 other teams with whom to chase 500 homers.

Bold Prediction: Stanton ends up with the San Diego Padres and finishes with 470 career home runs.

Who (If Anyone) Will Replace Stanton in New York?

He's not the most interesting option for the Yankees, but Goodman is the right guy for them.

Unless they want to trust in Austin Wells' recent surge to a .571 OPS, upgrading at catcher needs to be a priority. There will also be more time to reason with the Colorado Rockies, who were reportedly pushing for No. 1 prospects in Goodman talks before the deadline.

Bold Prediction: Goodman goes to the Yankees for a package of SS Dax Kilby, RHP Carlos Lagrange .

Statistics courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.title: Ranking MLB's Top 10 AL and NL MVP Candidates For 2026
articles.summary: For the past couple seasons, it's seemed like a competition to see who would be runner-up in both AL and NL MVP voting.
articles.body:
For the past couple seasons, it's seemed like a competition to see who would be runner-up in both AL and NL MVP voting.

In the AL, Aaron Judge won AL MVP in 2024 and 2025, his second and third AL MVP Awards, respectively.

After Shohei Ohtani won AL MVP as a member of the Los Angeles Angels in 2021 and 2023, the two-way superstar joined the Dodgers on a 10-year, $700 million deal.

All he did was win NL MVP in each of his first two seasons with the Dodgers, becoming just the second player in MLB history to win four MVPs (Barry Bonds won a staggering seven).

This year is shaping up to be different, though.

Judge is not going to win another AL MVP this season, as a stress fracture in his right ribcage has prevented him from playing since late-May.

Ohtani is still very much in the NL MVP race. For many years, though, it's felt like he's broken the award in the sense that if he plays, he's going to win it.

However, left knee inflammation has kept him from pitching since July 3. His offensive numbers remain elite, but not quite as staggering as his first two seasons with the Dodgers. So, there's at least a race in the NL in 2026.

With all that acknowledged, here are the top 10 AL and NL MVP candidates currently.

2026 Stats: .270 BA, 30 HR, 85 RBI, .860 OPS, 3.7 WAR

Since the All-Star Game, Pete Alonso is second among all American League hitters in OPS and third in WAR, according to FanGraphs . Alonso is one of the main reasons that the Orioles are still alive in a very weak AL wild-card race.

Regardless of how the rest of the season plays out for the O's, they have to be thrilled with the early returns on the five-year, $155 million deal they gave Alonso in free agency last offseason.

New York Mets' president of baseball operations David Stearns may never live down letting the greatest home run hitter in franchise history walk in free agency.

2026 Stats: .289 BA, 16 HR, 66 RBI, .792 OPS, 4.2 WAR

Despite having a 37-47 record at the end of June, the Red Sox are almost certainly going to be one of the AL's wild-card representatives. Ceddanne Rafaela has been at the forefront of a magical turnaround.

Per FanGraphs , Rafaela is sixth among all position players in WAR this season, which isn't surprising given how good of an all-around player he is.

The 25-year-old's calling card continues to be his center field glove, as he has 19 defensive runs saved and 14 outs above average in 2026.

2026 Stats: .245 BA, 29 HR, 74 RBI, .854 OPS, 4.4 WAR

Two years after losing a staggering 121 games, the White Sox find themselves in first place in the AL Central as the regular season begins to wind down. Miguel Vargas is one of the stars who has emerged during what's been a special season on the South Side.

Vargas leads the AL in runs scored, and is on the doorstep of his first 30-home run season. The 26-year-old was a first-time All-Star in 2026, and hit a titanic home run as part of the AL's victory at Citizens Bank Park:

There were some who felt badly for Vargas when he was traded by the Los Angeles Dodgers to the White Sox in July of 2024. As it turns out, getting to Chicago where he's had extended runway to play has been the best thing that could have happened for his career.

7. Willson Contreras: 1B, Boston Red Sox

2026 Stats: .282 BA, 26 HR, 78 RBI, .925 OPS, 4.0 WAR

Chief baseball officer Craig Breslow hit on the addition of Willson Contreras last offseason, acquiring him in a December trade from the St. Louis Cardinals.

Contreras' age-34 season has been arguably the finest of his decorated career, as he is second among all AL hitters in OPS .

Contreras' $17 million salary for 2027 looks like a bargain now, and heck, the $20 million club option the Red Sox have on him for 2028 looks downright affordable considering how he's performing.

2026 Stats: .253 BA, 26 HR, 82 RBI, .802 OPS, 5.0 WAR

Dillon Dingler has been the best catcher in baseball in 2026, providing both power production and great defensive numbers, with nine defensive runs saved and an 11 Fielding Run Value, per Statcast .

Shea Langeliers was voted the starter for the AL All-Star team over Dingler. However, with a WAR that's third among AL position players, it's hard to argue that anyone has played the position better than him in 2026, AL or NL.

2026 Stats: 8-5, 2.37 ERA, 2.39 FIP, 209 SO, 144.1 IP, 5.0 WAR

While the Blue Jays are still alive in the weakest American League playoff race in a generation, it's fair to say that it's been a very disappointing season for the defending Junior Circuit champions.

Dylan Cease has been tremendous, though, putting him very much in the AL Cy Young Award race after he joined the Jays on a seven-year, $210 million contract in free agency last offseason.

At the time of publication, Cease is tied for the highest WAR among AL starting pitchers, while leading the AL in strikeouts, FIP, H/9, HR/9 and K/9.

4. Cam Schlittler: RHP, New York Yankees

2026 Stats: 11-6, 2.16 ERA, 2.61 FIP, 193 SO, 158 IP, 5.0 WAR

Cam Schlittler is currently the front-runner to win the AL Cy Young Award, leading the junior circuit in ERA and ERA+ , while being tied with the aforementioned Cease for the top mark in WAR . Particularly in a weak AL, that puts him in line for some down-ballot MVP votes.

Perhaps the only concern with Schlittler is how he'll hold up in the final weeks of the regular season. This is his first full MLB season, and he's logged 158 innings pitched so far. Will he hit a wall in September? So far, there's no evidence of that, as Schlittler has a 2.52 ERA in seven starts since his first All-Star Game selection.

2026 Stats: .276 BA, 35 HR, 83 RBI, .895 OPS, 4.0 WAR

Junior Caminero has followed up a 45-homer season with an even better overall campaign, improving his OPS 50 points from the .846 mark he finished 2025 with.

When you add in that the Rays are likely to be the No. 1-seeded team in the AL playoff bracket, Caminero should be able to improve upon the ninth-place finish he had in AL MVP voting in 2025.

2. Bobby Witt Jr.: SS, Kansas City Royals

2026 Stats: .287 BA, 16 HR, 48 RBI, .822 OPS, 6.2 WAR

Bobby Witt Jr. is likely headed for his second AL MVP runner-up finish in three years, as he was second to the aforementioned Judge in 2024. 2026 will be the third consecutive top-four finish for Witt.

Witt doesn't put up the gaudy home run numbers that a typical AL MVP candidate will, but he leads all junior circuit players in WAR because he does pretty much everything well. In addition to 26 doubles and 34 stolen bases, Witt has eight defensive runs saved and a staggering 23 outs above average at shortstop.

There will likely be a day where Witt wins the AL MVP. In the meantime, three top-four finishes in as many seasons is a pretty nice start to a Hall of Fame resume.

1. Yordan Alvarez: DH/LF, Houston Astros

2026 Stats: .320 BA, 36 HR, 90 RBI, 1.049 OPS, 5.8 WAR

Yordan Alvarez was limited to just 48 games last season. He's returned in 2026 with a season that's trending towards netting him his first AL MVP Award. A third-place finish in 2022 is his highest to this point.

Not only is Alvarez currently in line to win the Triple Crown as the AL leader in batting average, RBI and home runs, but he also tops the Junior Circuit in on-base percentage, slugging percentage, OPS, OPS+, intentional walks and total bases.

10. Jordan Walker: RF, St. Louis Cardinals

2026 Stats: .289 BA, 27 HR, 96 RBI, .854 OPS, 3.3 WAR

Jordan Walker has gone from looking like a bust to one of the better players in baseball this season.

In a breakout season that saw him earn his first All-Star Game selection and win the Home Run Derby, Walker has demonstrated across-the-board improvements. He's gone from a dismal .584 OPS in 2025 to .857 in 2026. He still hasn't graded out great in right field, but the minus-three defensive runs saved he has in 2026 are much better than the minus-11 he had in 2025. And frankly, he's hitting well enough to justify a move to first base or DH in the future if that's what ultimately winds up happening.

Still just 24 years old, Walker looks like a building block for the Cardinals, alongside likely NL Rookie of the Year JJ Wetherholt, who just missed out on this list. Walker also edged out other sluggers like Matt Olson and Kyle Schwarber to nab this spot. That could very well change during the final month of the season.

9. Corbin Carroll: RF, Arizona Diamondbacks

2026 Stats: .250 BA, 18 HR, 57 RBI, .834 OPS, 4.4 WAR

Corbin Carroll finished fifth in NL MVP voting in 2023, and sixth in 2025. The lightning-fast outfielder is likely headed for a third top-10 finish in MVP voting in four seasons.

Carroll is leading baseball in triples. It would be the third year in a row he led baseball in triples, and the fourth straight where he topped the NL.

Additionally, Carroll has had his finest defensive season of his career, with 12 defensive runs saved and 10 outs above average in right field.

2026 Stats: .306 BA, 9 HR, 58 RBI, .787 OPS, 4.5 WAR

There will be some gripes that Otto López is on this list over some players with more power production and/or that play in bigger markets, but he deserves to be here.

A first-time All-Star in 2026, he is currently tied for second in WAR among NL position players, he's got four defensive runs saved and 10 outs above average at shortstop, a premium position. His .306 batting average is fourth among senior circuit hitters, while López has also managed to swipe 25 bases.

Again, there are some tremendous players who just missed this list. That's the nature of these types of exercises. In our estimation, though, López deserved to be here.

2026 Stats: 12-9, 2.20 ERA, 2.24 FIP, 166 SO, 4.9 WAR

Between 2020 and 2023, injuries limited Chris Sale to just 151 innings total, seeming to derail a career that had once seemed destined for Cooperstown.

However, he's now made the NL All-Star team three times in as many seasons with the Braves. He's unlikely to take home his second NL Cy Young Award in three seasons, but Sale will probably be a finalist. If he finishes anywhere in the top five, it will be the eighth time in his Hall of Fame-bound career that he's done that.

Sale finished seventh in NL MVP voting two years ago when he won the pitching Triple Crown, so some won't like that he's in the top 10 at all. But he's so dominant every five days that we'll live with flack from those who are against pitchers getting MVP votes.

6. CJ Abrams: SS/2B, Washington Nationals

2026 Stats: .279 BA, 29 HR, 91 RBI, .884 OPS, 3.8 WAR

CJ Abrams started at shortstop for the National League All-Star team thanks to a monster offensive season that has him trending towards hitting 30-plus homers and driving in over 100 runs, while posting an OPS above .875.

The Nationals have since moved Abrams to second base. It's too early to tell how effective he'll be at second base, but given that he had minus-10 defensive runs saved and minus-63 outs above average at shortstop in his career, it was probably the right move.

Regardless of where Abrams plays defensively, he has a special bat. It will be interesting to see how the Nationals proceed with him this offseason after a top-10 NL MVP finish. They could try to sign him to a long-term deal, or consider selling high on him and trading him with two years until free agency.

5. Cristopher Sánchez: LHP, Philadelphia Phillies

2026 Stats: 16-4, 2.62 ERA, 2.62 FIP, 194 SO, 168.1 IP, 5.4 WAR

Cristopher Sánchez didn't allow a single run across five starts during May, ultimately setting a new consecutive scoreless innings streak for a left-handed pitcher at 50.2 innings, which is the fifth-longest in MLB history.

Because of the emergence of another superstar pitcher in the NL, Sánchez will likely have to settle for his second consecutive runner-up finish in senior circuit Cy Young voting.

It's nonetheless been a special season for the 29-year-old lefty, who has cemented his place as one of baseball's top workhorses with a third consecutive tremendous campaign.

2026 Stats: .265 BA, 30 HR, 73 RBI, .928 OPS, 4.2 WAR

James Wood likely won't finish this high because he's been sidelined by a left oblique strain since Aug. 4. Still, based on what's taken place in the season to this point, he deserves to be this high.

Wood currently leads the senior circuit in on-base percentage (.393), and all of baseball in runs scored (100), despite the fact that he hasn't played in a few weeks. The Nationals have faded in his absence, but overachieved for much of the season thanks to an elite offense led by the 23-year-old.

The Nationals would be wise to try to sign Wood to a long-term extension this offseason. He'll become arbitration eligible in 2028, and can become a free agent after the 2030 campaign.

3. Jacob Misiorowski: RHP, Milwaukee Brewers

2026 Stats: 13-5, 1.68 ERA, 2.14 FIP, 216 SO, 145 IP, 5.6 WAR

The dominance of Jacob Misiorowski has probably been the story of the 2026 season, so you can argue he should be even higher on this list. Alas, a unanimous NL Cy Young victory and being an MVP finalist isn't a bad consolation prize.

"The Miz" leads all MLB starters in ERA, ERA+, strikeouts, FIP, WHIP, H/9, K/9, strikeout-to-walk ratio and WAR . It's hard to be much more dominant than that.

Of course, Misiorowski has done all this while averaging 100.6 mph on his fastball. It is fair to question how long he can consistently throw that hard, but he has held up this season, and it's been special to watch.

2. Shohei Ohtani: DH/RHP, Los Angeles Dodgers

2026 Batting Stats: .288 BA, 30 HR, 80 RBI, .935 OPS, 4.1 WAR

2026 Pitching Stats: 8-2, 1.79 ERA, 2.59 FIP, 95 SO, 85.2 IP, 3.0 WAR

Prior to his knee injury—and just an insane run from the guy at No. 1—Shohei Ohtani seemed destined to win his fifth MVP. And he still could depending on how the final month of the season goes.

There's no doubt, though, that Ohtani not pitching since July has hindered his MVP case. With an 8-2 record and 1.79 ERA in 14 starts, Ohtani was having his finest season on the mound yet. Had anything like that continued, it would have been hard to deny him the MVP.

Still, Ohtani has logged 85.2 innings and leads all NL hitters in OPS. This isn't his best season, but it's still pretty remarkable. And if his floor is finishing runner-up in MVP voting, that's a pretty great endorsement of his greatness.

1. Pete Crow-Armstrong: CF, Chicago Cubs

2026 Stats: .281 BA, 33 HR, 83 RBI, .938 OPS, 8.6 WAR

When Pete Crow-Armstrong had a .669 OPS at the end of April, there were serious questions about just how good of an offensive player he was. Mind you, this was on the heels of a .634 OPS after an All-Star selection in 2025.

Well, PCA has answered any questions about his offense since then, as he's leading the National League in both slugging percentage and total bases. It's also not an exaggeration to say he's one of the most gifted center field defenders we've ever seen, as he's headed towards a second consecutive Gold Glove Award win with 14 defensive runs saved and 23 outs above average.

Crow-Armstrong's 8.6 WAR is indicative of what's been one of the most complete seasons in recent memory. He's trending towards becoming the first Cub to win NL MVP since Kris Bryant in 2016.
paragraphs: For the past couple seasons, it's seemed like a competition to see who would be runner-up in both AL and NL MVP voting.
In the AL, Aaron Judge won AL MVP in 2024 and 2025, his second and third AL MVP Awards, respectively.
After Shohei Ohtani won AL MVP as a member of the Los Angeles Angels in 2021 and 2023, the two-way superstar joined the Dodgers on a 10-year, $700 million deal.
All he did was win NL MVP in each of his first two seasons with the Dodgers, becoming just the second player in MLB history to win four MVPs (Barry Bonds won a staggering seven).
This year is shaping up to be different, though.
Judge is not going to win another AL MVP this season, as a stress fracture in his right ribcage has prevented him from playing since late-May.
Ohtani is still very much in the NL MVP race. For many years, though, it's felt like he's broken the award in the sense that if he plays, he's going to win it.

However, left knee inflammation has kept him from pitching since July 3. His offensive numbers remain elite, but not quite as staggering as his first two seasons with the Dodgers. So, there's at least a race in the NL in 2026.
With all that acknowledged, here are the top 10 AL and NL MVP candidates currently.
2026 Stats: .270 BA, 30 HR, 85 RBI, .860 OPS, 3.7 WAR

Since the All-Star Game, Pete Alonso is second among all American League hitters in OPS and third in WAR, according to FanGraphs . Alonso is one of the main reasons that the Orioles are still alive in a very weak AL wild-card race.
Regardless of how the rest of the season plays out for the O's, they have to be thrilled with the early returns on the five-year, $155 million deal they gave Alonso in free agency last offseason.
New York Mets' president of baseball operations David Stearns may never live down letting the greatest home run hitter in franchise history walk in free agency.
2026 Stats: .289 BA, 16 HR, 66 RBI, .792 OPS, 4.2 WAR

Despite having a 37-47 record at the end of June, the Red Sox are almost certainly going to be one of the AL's wild-card representatives. Ceddanne Rafaela has been at the forefront of a magical turnaround.
Per FanGraphs , Rafaela is sixth among all position players in WAR this season, which isn't surprising given how good of an all-around player he is.
The 25-year-old's calling card continues to be his center field glove, as he has 19 defensive runs saved and 14 outs above average in 2026.
2026 Stats: .245 BA, 29 HR, 74 RBI, .854 OPS, 4.4 WAR

Two years after losing a staggering 121 games, the White Sox find themselves in first place in the AL Central as the regular season begins to wind down. Miguel Vargas is one of the stars who has emerged during what's been a special season on the South Side.

Vargas leads the AL in runs scored, and is on the doorstep of his first 30-home run season. The 26-year-old was a first-time All-Star in 2026, and hit a titanic home run as part of the AL's victory at Citizens Bank Park:

There were some who felt badly for Vargas when he was traded by the Los Angeles Dodgers to the White Sox in July of 2024. As it turns out, getting to Chicago where he's had extended runway to play has been the best thing that could have happened for his career.
7. Willson Contreras: 1B, Boston Red Sox
2026 Stats: .282 BA, 26 HR, 78 RBI, .925 OPS, 4.0 WAR
Chief baseball officer Craig Breslow hit on the addition of Willson Contreras last offseason, acquiring him in a December trade from the St. Louis Cardinals.
Contreras' age-34 season has been arguably the finest of his decorated career, as he is second among all AL hitters in OPS .
Contreras' $17 million salary for 2027 looks like a bargain now, and heck, the $20 million club option the Red Sox have on him for 2028 looks downright affordable considering how he's performing.
2026 Stats: .253 BA, 26 HR, 82 RBI, .802 OPS, 5.0 WAR
Dillon Dingler has been the best catcher in baseball in 2026, providing both power production and great defensive numbers, with nine defensive runs saved and an 11 Fielding Run Value, per Statcast .

Shea Langeliers was voted the starter for the AL All-Star team over Dingler. However, with a WAR that's third among AL position players, it's hard to argue that anyone has played the position better than him in 2026, AL or NL.

While the Blue Jays are still alive in the weakest American League playoff race in a generation, it's fair to say that it's been a very disappointing season for the defending Junior Circuit champions.
Dylan Cease has been tremendous, though, putting him very much in the AL Cy Young Award race after he joined the Jays on a seven-year, $210 million contract in free agency last offseason.
At the time of publication, Cease is tied for the highest WAR among AL starting pitchers, while leading the AL in strikeouts, FIP, H/9, HR/9 and K/9.
4. Cam Schlittler: RHP, New York Yankees

Cam Schlittler is currently the front-runner to win the AL Cy Young Award, leading the junior circuit in ERA and ERA+ , while being tied with the aforementioned Cease for the top mark in WAR . Particularly in a weak AL, that puts him in line for some down-ballot MVP votes.

Perhaps the only concern with Schlittler is how he'll hold up in the final weeks of the regular season. This is his first full MLB season, and he's logged 158 innings pitched so far. Will he hit a wall in September? So far, there's no evidence of that, as Schlittler has a 2.52 ERA in seven starts since his first All-Star Game selection.
2026 Stats: .276 BA, 35 HR, 83 RBI, .895 OPS, 4.0 WAR

In addition to 26 doubles and 34 stolen bases, Witt has eight defensive runs saved and a staggering 23 outs above average at shortstop.
There will likely be a day where Witt wins the AL MVP. In the meantime, three top-four finishes in as many seasons is a pretty nice start to a Hall of Fame resume.
1. Yordan Alvarez: DH/LF, Houston Astros
2026 Stats: .320 BA, 36 HR, 90 RBI, 1.049 OPS, 5.8 WAR

Yordan Alvarez was limited to just 48 games last season. He's returned in 2026 with a season that's trending towards netting him his first AL MVP Award. A third-place finish in 2022 is his highest to this point.

Not only is Alvarez currently in line to win the Triple Crown as the AL leader in batting average, RBI and home runs, but he also tops the Junior Circuit in on-base percentage, slugging percentage, OPS, OPS+, intentional walks and total bases.
10. Jordan Walker: RF, St. Louis Cardinals
2026 Stats: .289 BA, 27 HR, 96 RBI, .854 OPS, 3.3 WAR
Jordan Walker has gone from looking like a bust to one of the better players in baseball this season.

In a breakout season that saw him earn his first All-Star Game selection and win the Home Run Derby, Walker has demonstrated across-the-board improvements. He's gone from a dismal .584 OPS in 2025 to .857 in 2026. He still hasn't graded out great in right field, but the minus-three defensive runs saved he has in 2026 are much better than the minus-11 he had in 2025. And frankly, he's hitting well enough to justify a move to first base or DH in the future if that's what ultimately winds up happening.

Still just 24 years old, Walker looks like a building block for the Cardinals, alongside likely NL Rookie of the Year JJ Wetherholt, who just missed out on this list. Walker also edged out other sluggers like Matt Olson and Kyle Schwarber to nab this spot. That could very well change during the final month of the season.
9. Corbin Carroll: RF, Arizona Diamondbacks
2026 Stats: .250 BA, 18 HR, 57 RBI, .834 OPS, 4.4 WAR
Corbin Carroll finished fifth in NL MVP voting in 2023, and sixth in 2025. The lightning-fast outfielder is likely headed for a third top-10 finish in MVP voting in four seasons.
Carroll is leading baseball in triples. It would be the third year in a row he led baseball in triples, and the fourth straight where he topped the NL.
Additionally, Carroll has had his finest defensive season of his career, with 12 defensive runs saved and 10 outs above average in right field.
2026 Stats: .306 BA, 9 HR, 58 RBI, .787 OPS, 4.5 WAR
There will be some gripes that Otto López is on this list over some players with more power production and/or that play in bigger markets, but he deserves to be here.

A first-time All-Star in 2026, he is currently tied for second in WAR among NL position players, he's got four defensive runs saved and 10 outs above average at shortstop, a premium position. His .306 batting average is fourth among senior circuit hitters, while López has also managed to swipe 25 bases.
Again, there are some tremendous players who just missed this list. That's the nature of these types of exercises. In our estimation, though, López deserved to be here.
Between 2020 and 2023, injuries limited Chris Sale to just 151 innings total, seeming to derail a career that had once seemed destined for Cooperstown.

However, he's now made the NL All-Star team three times in as many seasons with the Braves. He's unlikely to take home his second NL Cy Young Award in three seasons, but Sale will probably be a finalist. If he finishes anywhere in the top five, it will be the eighth time in his Hall of Fame-bound career that he's done that.

Sale finished seventh in NL MVP voting two years ago when he won the pitching Triple Crown, so some won't like that he's in the top 10 at all. But he's so dominant every five days that we'll live with flack from those who are against pitchers getting MVP votes.
6. CJ Abrams: SS/2B, Washington Nationals
2026 Stats: .279 BA, 29 HR, 91 RBI, .884 OPS, 3.8 WAR

CJ Abrams started at shortstop for the National League All-Star team thanks to a monster offensive season that has him trending towards hitting 30-plus homers and driving in over 100 runs, while posting an OPS above .875.

The Nationals have since moved Abrams to second base. It's too early to tell how effective he'll be at second base, but given that he had minus-10 defensive runs saved and minus-63 outs above average at shortstop in his career, it was probably the right move.

Regardless of where Abrams plays defensively, he has a special bat. It will be interesting to see how the Nationals proceed with him this offseason after a top-10 NL MVP finish. They could try to sign him to a long-term deal, or consider selling high on him and trading him with two years until free agency.
5. Cristopher Sánchez: LHP, Philadelphia Phillies

Cristopher Sánchez didn't allow a single run across five starts during May, ultimately setting a new consecutive scoreless innings streak for a left-handed pitcher at 50.2 innings, which is the fifth-longest in MLB history.
Because of the emergence of another superstar pitcher in the NL, Sánchez will likely have to settle for his second consecutive runner-up finish in senior circuit Cy Young voting.
It's nonetheless been a special season for the 29-year-old lefty, who has cemented his place as one of baseball's top workhorses with a third consecutive tremendous campaign.
2026 Stats: .265 BA, 30 HR, 73 RBI, .928 OPS, 4.2 WAR

James Wood likely won't finish this high because he's been sidelined by a left oblique strain since Aug. 4. Still, based on what's taken place in the season to this point, he deserves to be this high.

Wood currently leads the senior circuit in on-base percentage (.393), and all of baseball in runs scored (100), despite the fact that he hasn't played in a few weeks. The Nationals have faded in his absence, but overachieved for much of the season thanks to an elite offense led by the 23-year-old.

articles.title: Little League World Series 2026 Tuesday Schedule, TV Info and Bracket Predictions
articles.summary: Extra-innings thrillers dominated Monday's slate of action and resulted in the home state team's dreams of its first Little League World Series title in 66 years being dashed.
articles.body:
Extra-innings thrillers dominated Monday's slate of action and resulted in the home state team's dreams of its first Little League World Series title in 66 years being dashed.

The action continues Tuesday, with high-stakes games across the board as teams look to stave off elimination and keep their championship hopes alive.

Who plays when, who took to the diamond for the final time Monday, and when can viewers check out all of the action?

Find out with this preview of Tuesday's lineup.

Great Lakes Region: West Side LL (Hamilton, Ohio)

Metro Region: Bayonne Central LL (Bayonne, New Jersey)

Mid-Atlantic Region: East Side LL (West Chester, Pennsylvania)

Midwest Region: Davenport Northwest LL (Davenport, Iowa)

Mountain Region: Paseo Verde, LL (Henderson, Nevada)

New England Region: Bridgewater Joe Lozaro LL (Bridgewater, Massachusetts)

Northwest Region: Soundview LL (Tacoma, Washington)

Southeast Region: Phenix City Youth Baseball LL (Phenix City, Alabama)

Southwest Region: Boerne LL (Boerne, Texas)

West Region: Sweetwater Valley LL (Bonita, California)

Asian-Pacific Region: West Seoul (B) LL (Seoul, South Korea)

Australia Region: Ryde Little League (Sydney, New South Wales)

Canada Region: Little Mountain LLC (Vancouver, British Columbia)

Caribbean Region: Los Nacionales LL (Santiago, Dominican Republic)

Curaçao Region: Pariba LL (Willemstad, Curaçao)

Europe and Africa Region: South Czech Republic LL (Brno, Czechia)

Latin American Region: Ministerio Sobre Las Alas Del Aguila LL (Leon, Nicaragua)

Mexico Region: Municipal De Tijuana LL (Tijuana, Baja California)

Panama Region: David Doleguita LL (Chiriquí, Panama)

Game 25: Mexico vs. Japan (1:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: Japan)

Game 26: Northwest vs. Southeast (3:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: Southeast)

Game 27: Canada vs. Asia-Pacific (5:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: Asia-Pacific)

Game 28: Great Lakes vs. Metro (7:00 p.m., ESPN) (Prediction: Metro)

Pennsylvania Eliminated, Ohio Sends a Message

The Levittown team of 1960 will remain the last Pennsylvania team to win the Little League World Series, at least for now, after East Side Little League from West Chester was bounced from the tournament on Monday.

The loss came in extra innings, which was needed only because the host state conceded a five-run lead.

Pitcher Kinley Rasmus righted the ship for Alabama as she held East Side scoreless and Brooks Cameron delivered the game-winning RBI to keep the Phenix team in the hunt for a title.

Elsewhere, West Side Little League from Hamilton, Ohio, hung six runs on Boerne Little League from Texas, eliminating them and advancing to Tuesday's slate of games.

Overcoming a loss in their first game, the Ohio squad has won two straight, with its bats coming alive to put up 16 runs in their last two games.

articles.title: Merrill Kelly Calls 'Bulls--t' on Cubs 3B Coach for Potentially Stealing Signs in D-Backs Loss
articles.summary: After suffering a 7-0 loss to the Chicago Cubs on Monday night, Arizona Diamondbacks starting pitcher Merrill Kelly feels they had an unfair advantage.
articles.body:
After suffering a 7-0 loss to the Chicago Cubs on Monday night, Arizona Diamondbacks starting pitcher Merrill Kelly feels they had an unfair advantage.

Kelly, who gave up three earned runs in 5.2 innings pitched, had a confrontation on the field with Cubs third base coach Quintin Berry, whom he accused of stealing signs and relaying them to Chicago's hitters.

"Stealing signs is as old as baseball. I think it's a little bulls--t when it comes from a coach," Kelly told reporters after the game. "I think if it's a guy on second base and they see the grip in your glove, or if the hitters can see something that you're doing with your glove, I think that's fair game. I think guys have been doing that since the beginning of baseball. I think it's a little bush league when it comes from outside that. I think inside the lines is one thing, I think the guys standing outside the lines, I think it's a little bush league."

While Kelly acknowledged that coaches sometimes get in on the sign-stealing strategy, he said Berry's actions on Monday were "the most egregious I've seen from coaches."

Kelly is now 8-12 with a career-worst 5.35 ERA, giving up a combined 15 runs over his last three starts. The 37-year-old veteran admitted that he needs to adjust going forward so the Diamondbacks can avoid being at a disadvantage again.

"That being said, I gotta take a look at what I'm doing, because clearly he had something. And obviously, if he has it, then other people will probably pick up on it as well," Kelly said. "So I gotta do better on my part to not give it away. But yeah, I think it should stay between the players."

articles.title: Who is Kinley Rasmus? Meet the Phenix City girl starring at Little League World Series
articles.summary: "I've enjoyed every single second of this whole opportunity. I'm so grateful that I get to be in this position because I know many are wishing to be here, an...
articles.body:
Viewers across the world cannot get enough of Phenix City Little League sensation Kinley Rasmus. The 12-year-old has been dominant this summer en route to helping her team clinch a Southeast Regional title and a top-six finish, at minimum, in the United States at the Little League World Series. Her all-around play and general demeanor has made her a viral star that will not soon fade.

It didn't take long for her parents Cory, a former Major League Baseball pitcher and member of the famed Rasmus baseball family that won the U.S. title at the 1999 LLWS, and Jill, a former Division I softball player at Southern Mississippi whose brother, Jeff, was an MLB catcher, to realize that Kinley was talented.

"It's our daughter, so we always probably have looked at her maybe even a little as better than she might have been," Cory said. "But at the same time, we love her, we pull for her, and she's found a way. Even at 5 and 6 years old, she played, and she's always been this even-keeled kid that really isn't afraid of the moment. So for her to continue to keep getting better and keep performing in big moments, it almost seems like nothing bothers her. It's crazy to watch, but obviously we're super proud."

Kinley is one of 25 girls to have played in the 79-year history of the LLWS. The eight strikeouts she threw in Phenix City's opening LLWS game tied the record for most by a girl. Her total of 14 strikeouts thrown so far also ties the tournament record for a girl. She is just the fifth gir l to notch multiple hits in the LLWS — and the first to produce an extra-base hit . And she has made sparkling defensive plays in the field.

But don't get it twisted. Kinley isn't just good at baseball for a girl. Kinley has proven to be one of the very best 12U baseball players in all of America.

After her dramatic, terrific performance on the mound Monday night in the team's come-from-behind win against Pennsylvania, 6-5, Rasmus has thrown 26 ⅔ innings this summer and allowed just three earned runs, good for an ERA of 0.70. She has walked just three batters. Three walks in 26 ⅔ innings would be elite at any level of baseball. It's simply unheard of for a 12-year-old to do it.

After she fired a shutout in the team's Southeast Regional final win over Nolensville, Tennessee, two weeks ago, buzz about Rasmus started to build in the Little League World Series. Then she threw six shutout, one-hit innings against Northwest in an eventual extra-inning loss after she left the game due to pitch count regulations. A two-hit performance, including a double off the left-field wall and some slick defensive plays followed against the West representative, Sweetwater Valley Little League out of Bonita California, on Saturday.

Her stardom reached a higher level with Monday's virtuoso performance. Coming in to pitch with her team down 5-0 with one out in the third inning, she fired 4 ⅔ innings of shutout ball, made two terrific defensive plays and drove in the tying run to help Phenix City stave off elimination against East Side Little League from West Chester. Pennsylvania.

She has been handling that newfound fame with an ease that shows maturity far beyond her age. If Kinley signed every autograph, did every interview and took every picture that people wanted at the Little League World Series Complex, she would be doing nothing else during her LLWS experience. But she has tried to do as much as she can without letting her play suffer on the field.

"I've enjoyed every single second of this whole opportunity," Kinley said. "I'm so grateful that I get to be in this position because I know many are wishing to be here, and I'm just so grateful to be here."

Jill has been handling a lot of the media requests that come in, which are well into the dozens at this point.

"We definitely didn't know what to expect coming in," Jill said. "You know, like she said, definitely grateful to be here. It's a cool opportunity, but also, as her parents, just to try to know when to draw the line or when she's had enough. But at the same time, a lot of little kids are looking up to her, and I try to push her to do things out of her comfort zone.

"I think it's good for her to get out and talk to people and do these interviews, even though she may not want to.I feel like I know when enough is enough. I can tell when she's tired or gets tired of it, and I feel like we can kind of draw the line and do which ones are best or whatever."

Kinley doesn't just excel on the baseball diamond. In fact, this Little League World Series is likely the last baseball tournament she will ever play in. She has been splitting time with softball for years now and projects to be one of, if not the best, recruits in the class of 2032. And she will be the starting quarterback for the top-in-the-nation Central-Phenix City High School flag football team this fall, when she gets back from Williamsport, that is.

She is undecided on which sport she wants to play in college, but she will have no shortage of suitors.

Kinley's trademark hair bow has become a trending topic, with Phenix City fans chanting, "Fear the bow" and plenty of signs featuring the phrase at Lamade Stadium. paragraphs: Viewers across the world cannot get enough of Phenix City Little League sensation Kinley Rasmus. The 12-year-old has been dominant this summer en route to helping her team clinch a Southeast Regional title and a top-six finish, at minimum, in the United States at the Little League World Series. Her all-around play and general demeanor has made her a viral star that will not soon fade.

It didn't take long for her parents Cory, a former Major League Baseball pitcher and member of the famed Rasmus baseball family that won the U.S. title at the 1999 LLWS, and Jill, a former Division I softball player at Southern Mississippi whose brother, Jeff, was an MLB catcher, to realize that Kinley was talented.

"It's our daughter, so we always probably have looked at her maybe even a little as better than she might have been," Cory said. "But at the same time, we love her, we pull for her, and she's found a way. Even at 5 and 6 years old, she played, and she's always been this even-keeled kid that really isn't afraid of the moment. So for her to continue to keep getting better and keep performing in big moments, it almost seems like nothing bothers her. It's crazy to watch, but obviously we're super proud."

Kinley is one of 25 girls to have played in the 79-year history of the LLWS. The eight strikeouts she threw in Phenix City's opening LLWS game tied the record for most by a girl. Her total of 14 strikeouts thrown so far also ties the tournament record for a girl. She is just the fifth gir l to notch multiple hits in the LLWS — and the first to produce an extra-base hit . And she has made sparkling defensive plays in the field.
But don't get it twisted. Kinley isn't just good at baseball for a girl. Kinley has proven to be one of the very best 12U baseball players in all of America.

After her dramatic, terrific performance on the mound Monday night in the team's come-from-behind win against Pennsylvania, 6-5, Rasmus has thrown 26 ⅔ innings this summer and allowed just three earned runs, good for an ERA of 0.70. She has walked just three batters. Three walks in 26 ⅔ innings would be elite at any level of baseball. It's simply unheard of for a 12-year-old to do it.

Then she threw six shutout, one-hit innings against Northwest in an eventual extra-inning loss after she left the game due to pitch count regulations. A two-hit performance, including a double off the left-field wall and some slick defensive plays followed against the West representative, Sweetwater Valley Little League out of Bonita California, on Saturday.

Pennsylvania.

She has been handling that newfound fame with an ease that shows maturity far beyond her age. If Kinley signed every autograph, did every interview and took every picture that people wanted at the Little League World Series Complex, she would be doing nothing else during her LLWS experience. But she has tried to do as much as she can without letting her play suffer on the field.

"I've enjoyed every single second of this whole opportunity," Kinley said. "I'm so grateful that I get to be in this position because I know many are wishing to be here, and I'm just so grateful to be here."
Jill has been handling a lot of the media requests that come in, which are well into the dozens at this point.

articles.title: Blue Jays add SP Shane Bieber to IL, giving Toronto thin pitching depth in AL wild-card race
articles.summary: Bieber has a 5-2 record with a 4.53 ERA this season.
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays announced they have added starting pitcher Shane Bieber to the 15-day injured list. Bieber was added due to "right teres major inflammation," and the move is retroactive to Aug. 21.

For clarity, the injury is inflammation of the right teres major, not major inflammation of the right teres. This means that Bieber is dealing with inflammation in the thick muscle on his right side, in the upper back and shoulder.

Bieber has pitched in only 11 games this season. He had Tommy John surgery at the end of last season, and it caused him to miss 78 games at the beginning of the season.

Since his activation from the IL, the veteran has posted a 5-2 record with a 4.53 ERA. Bieber has struck out 44 batters in 55.2 innings of work. While he hasn't been pitching as dominantly as he had in stretches during his time with the Cleveland Guardians , he has shifted more into a veteran role, called on to pitch reliably but not expected to be the franchise's ace.

Cal Raleigh busts out of slump, posts first career 3-homer game to power Mariners past Phillies

Ketel Marte lost the benefit of the doubt long before he showed up to the casino

Mariners shortstop Colt Emerson to have season-ending surgery on left wrist

Bieber's injury forces Toronto to add another starting pitcher to the IL. He joins Trey Yesavage , who has been sidelined since Aug. 4 due to a knee injury. The latest update on Yesavage came a week ago, and he had begun to throw on flat ground as he ramped up his activity.

As of Bieber's addition to the IL, Toronto has a 64-68 record and is in fourth place in the AL East. Despite the losing record, the Blue Jays are only two games back of the third wild-card spot in the American League.

With a little over a month left in the regular season, there is time for Toronto to make a playoff push, but the Blue Jays would likely feel better about it if their starting pitchers were able to get healthy sooner rather than later.

articles.title: Resumen y carreras México vs Japón Serie Mundial de Pequeñas Ligas: Dos errores condenan a Tijuana en Williamsport
articles.standfirst: La Liga Municipal de Tijuana se despidió de la Serie Mundial de Pequeñas Ligas 2026 después de un juego en el que dejó escapar oportunidades con corredores en base.
articles.summary: La Liga Municipal de Tijuana se despidió de la Serie Mundial de Pequeñas Ligas 2026 después de un juego en el que dejó escapar oportunidades con corredores en base.
articles.body: El sueño de México en Williamsport terminó frente a un viejo conocido. La Liga Municipal de Tijuana tuvo oportunidades para cambiar la historia, llenó las bases desde la primera entrada y consiguió mantenerse con vida hasta el tramo final, pero Japón aprovechó mejor sus momentos y se impuso 3-1 en un partido de eliminación directa de la Serie Mundial de Pequeñas Ligas 2026. La diferencia comenzó a construirse desde el primer inning, cuando dos errores defensivos mexicanos permitieron las primeras dos carreras japonesas. México respondió desde el montículo con Jorge Fonseca y encontró una carrera para acercarse, pero la ofensiva nunca terminó de descifrar al pitcheo nipón, que fue apagando cualquier intento de remontada. Jorge Fonseca comenzó como pitcher de México, pero Japón atacó desde el inicio. Después de colocar un corredor en primera, Tensei Yazawa conectó un hit para dejar hombres en primera y segunda sin outs. El primer daño llegó con un error del jardinero izquierdo mexicano que permitió el 1-0 de Japón. Poco después, otra equivocación defensiva, ahora de Néstor Melchor, abrió la puerta para el 2-0. México evitó que el golpe fuera todavía mayor con una buena intervención de Óscar Mateo Montañez que ayudó a concretar una doble matanza. La respuesta mexicana estuvo muy cerca. Matías García y Fonseca conectaron imparables, mientras Gareth García recibió base por bolas. México tuvo las bases llenas, pero Rafael Mesina fue ponchado y Emiliano Kerber tampoco logró producir. La primera gran oportunidad se escapó. Fonseca se recuperó del complicado comienzo y encontró estabilidad. articles.title: Little League World Series 2026 Tuesday Scores, Bracket Results and Highlights
articles.summary: The bottom half of the bracket continued to progress at the Little League World Series in Williamsport on Tuesday, with four teams set to remain alive and four bound to head home.
articles.body:
The bottom half of the bracket continued to progress at the Little League World Series in Williamsport on Tuesday, with four teams set to remain alive and four bound to head home.

Below we'll break down the day's results and top highlights as the bracket comes further into focus.

Little League World Series 2026 Monday Schedule, TV Info and Bracket Predictions

Tensei Yazawa's fantastic pitching performance, paired with Ryosuke Takaoka's two RBI, led Japan to a 3-1 victory over Mexico on Tuesday.

Yazawa pitched five innings, allowing just four hits, two walks and a run while striking out seven. Rafael Mesina provided the lone RBI for Mexico.

Up next for Japan is a showdown with Canada.

Led by Jerry Taylor's strong afternoon on the mound, Southeast defeated Northwest on Tuesday, 4-2.

Taylor went five innings, giving up four hits and four walks but allowing just two runs, striking out three. Four different players for Southeast drove in runs in a balanced offensive effort.

Southeast will next face the winner of Great Lakes vs. Metro.

Led by Cruz Krpan's two hits, one run and one RBI, Canada defeated Asia-Pacific 5-1 on Tuesday.

Jean Ramos and Kian Sandhu combined to give up just one run on the mound, striking out five. Asia-Pacific managed to put 13 runners on base but was unable to better capitalize on those opportunities.

Up next for Canada is a matchup against Japan.

Great Lakes used a dominant fourth inning to advance to the next stage with a 5-2 win over Metro.

The victors pushed all five of their runs across in the fifth with Xander Kinkade driving in two with a double and then scoring another. Josiah Infante, Jack McAdams and Walker Osborne each added two hits as well.

Metro threatened in the final inning with a run before bringing the tying run to the plate, but Bryson Williams closed the door on the mound for the win.

He entered in relief of Boone Treadway after the starter allowed just two runs and struck out eight in five innings of work.

articles.title: What to Know About Kinley Rasmus' Family Tree Amid LLWS Star's Historic Performance
articles.summary: Kinley Rasmus has been a key contributor for Alabama's Phenix City Youth Baseball to start the 2026 Little League World Series.
articles.body:
Kinley Rasmus has been a key contributor for Alabama's Phenix City Youth Baseball to start the 2026 Little League World Series.

Rasmus' family has plenty of MLB experience, while her cousin is also her teammate.

Her father, Cory, helped lead Phenix City to the Little League World Series championship game in 1999 before pitching for the Atlanta Braves and Los Angeles Angels from 2013-16.

Kinley's uncle, Colby, appeared in 1,092 MLB games throughout his career from 2009-18.

Meanwhile, her grandfather coached the 1999 Phenix City team and was a former draft pick of the Angels. Her mother also played softball at Southern Mississippi.

Kinley has amassed 14 strikeouts in this year's tournament, tying Mo'ne Davis' Little League World Series record for strikeouts by a girl.

She revealed that she's looking to follow in her father's footsteps and help Phenix City contend for a Little League World Series title.

"I just always hear my dad talking about [Williamsport] and how much fun he had, and I just want to do the same thing," Kinley said, per ESPN's J.J. Post .

Through Alabama's first three Little League World Series contests in Williamsport, she went 3-for-7 at the plate. On the mound, she allowed just three hits without giving up an earned run in 10.2 innings pitched.

Alabama is in the midst of an impressive tournament run, coming back from a five-run deficit to secure a 6-5 victory over Pennsylvania on Monday.

Rasmus' squad ultimately advanced to face Washington in an elimination game on Tuesday.

articles.title: Kinley Rasmus Makes History, Final Box Score Stats, Highlights from LLWS Elimination Bracket
articles.summary: Kinley Rasmus and Phenix City, Alabama, continued their Little League World Series run on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Kinley Rasmus and Phenix City, Alabama, continued their Little League World Series run on Tuesday.

Phenix City, representing the Southeast region, defeated Northwest 4-2 in an elimination game.

Rasmus, who once again made history on the mound in her last time out, didn't pitch on Tuesday but went 2-for-3 with an RBI and a run in the win. With her second hit of the night, she broke the Little League World Series record for the most hits by a girl.

Southeast got on the board early with a run in the bottom of the first, and it then tacked on two more in the bottom of the third. Rasmus recorded an RBI single to put Southeast up 2-0, and Cam Lee then hit a double to drive her in.

Northwest answered with a run in the top of the fourth, but Southeast made it 4-1 in the bottom of the fourth when Ryker Rasmus, Kinley's cousin, drove in a run.

Northwest attempted to rally in the sixth and drove in one run, but it ultimately didn't have enough to survive in the elimination game.

With the win, Southeast will now play the winner of Great Lakes vs. Metro.

articles.title: NCAA Approves ABS Challenge System as Part of Rule Changes for 2027 Baseball Season
articles.summary: The NCAA announced on Tuesday that the automated ball-strike system has been approved for the next season of collegiate baseball at all levels, per the Associated Press.
articles.body:
The NCAA announced on Tuesday that the automated ball-strike system has been approved for the next season of collegiate baseball at all levels, per the Associated Press .

In May, the SEC tried out an ABS system during its conference tournament. Major League Baseball also added an ABS system and it has largely been seen as a positive addition to the sport.

At the MLB level, teams start with two challenges and only lose them if they unsuccessfully challenge a balls-and-strike call.

The NCAA will also allow for the use of 18-inch square bases, though 15-inch square bases will remain the standard, while a double first base will now be required.

At the Division I level, a 30-second timer will be employed between batters and for mound visits or offensive timeouts.
