articles.title: Merrill Kelly accuses Cubs coach Quintin Berry of sign stealing, calls move âbush leagueâ after heated clash
articles.summary: MLB News: Arizona Diamondbacks pitcher Merrill Kelly accused Chicago Cubs third-base coach Quintin Berry of stealing and relaying signs during Monday nightâs 7-.
articles.body: Arizona Diamondbacks pitcher Merrill Kelly accused Chicago Cubs third-base coach Quintin Berry of stealing and relaying signs during Monday nightâs 7-0 loss at Chase Field. Kelly said Berry appeared to have picked up something about his changeup and was passing that information to Cubs hitters, particularly left-handed batters. The accusation led to a heated exchange between the two dugouts in the fifth inning. After the game, Kelly made his view clear, saying sign stealing is part of baseball when players do it, but called it âa little bush leagueâ when a coach is involved. MLB also reported the incident.Merrill Kelly calls out Quintin Berry over sign-stealing accusationThe issue came up in the fifth inning when Kelly was pitching to Michael Busch with runners on base. Kelly stepped off the mound and looked toward Berry, who was standing in the Cubsâ third-base coaching box. The two benches then started shouting at each other as the Diamondbacks questioned whether Berry was picking up Kellyâs signs.Kelly later explained what Arizona believed was happening. He said the Diamondbacks thought Berry had noticed something about his changeup and was relaying it to Chicagoâs hitters.âStealing signs is as old as baseball,â Kelly said. âI think itâs a little bull**** when it comes from a coach.âI think if itâs a guy on second base and they see the grip in your glove or if the hitters can see something that youâre doing with your glove, I think thatâs fair game.âI think guys have been doing that since the beginning of baseball.âI think itâs a little bush league when it comes from outside that.âKelly did not say that stealing signs itself was wrong. Instead, he drew a line between what players can notice during a game and what he believes coaches should be doing from outside the field.Craig Counsell responds as Cubs beat DiamondbacksThe tension did not end when the fifth inning was over. Kelly was removed after allowing a two-out single in the sixth and appeared to stare toward Berry and the Cubsâ bench as he walked away.Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo had already stepped onto the mound earlier to settle things down and give Kelly a chance to finish the inning.Cubs manager Craig Counsell did not treat the incident as a major issue. After the game, he described it simply as âgamesmanship that goes on every day in the league.âKelly also accepted that he needs to look at his own pitching. If Berry really noticed something, Kelly said, other teams could potentially notice it too.âThat being said, I gotta take a look at what Iâm doing, because clearly he had something. And obviously if he has it, then other people would probably pick up on it as well. I gotta figure out and do better on my part to not give it away. But yeah, I think it should stay between the players.âThe Cubs finished the night with a 7-0 win, while Kelly gave up three earned runs over 5â  innings. The accusation now adds another layer to an already important late-season series between two teams fighting for a postseason spot.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: San Diego Padres Minor League Coach is Released From ICE Custody, Family Says
articles.summary: A San Diego Padres minor league coaching coordinator who was detained by federal immigration officers in Texas has been released on bond, his family said Tuesday.
articles.body:
A San Diego Padres minor league coaching coordinator who was detained by federal immigration officers in Texas has been released on bond, his family said Tuesday.

Oswaldo Pirela, who is from Venezuela and lives in Arizona, was back home with his family following his release on Monday, his sister Daniela Pirela said. The Padres also confirmed that Pirela, a catching coordinator in their minor league system, was no longer in custody.

"We are pleased that Oswaldo Pirela has been released on bond and reunited with his family. Out of respect for his privacy and the ongoing matter, we will have no further comment at this time," the team said in a statement.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained Pirela at the El Paso International Airport during a work trip on Aug. 16. The Padres have a minor league affiliate team in the city, the El Paso Chihuahuas.

The Department of Homeland Security has previously said Pirela came to the U.S. legally in 2014 and "overstayed his welcome" after 2018. His family has disputed Homeland Security's account and says Pirela had applied for asylum and obtained work permits.

On Tuesday, DHS said in a statement that Pirela was released on bond pending removal proceedings, adding that work authorization or a pending application do not "confer legal status."

Pirela had a brief minor-league playing career as a catcher in the Texas Rangers organization.

articles.title: Toronto Blue Jays Announce Roster Decision on 9-Year MLB Player During Royals Series
articles.summary: The Toronto Blue Jays are set to begin a three-game series with the Kansas City Royals on Tuesday, which is a much tougher task than it looks on paper. The R...
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays are set to begin a three-game series with the Kansas City Royals on Tuesday, which is a much tougher task than it looks on paper. The Royals are 9-1 over their last 10 games, while the Blue Jays are fresh off a series loss to the Yankees .

Despite being below .500, Toronto is still very much alive in the AL Wild Card standings.

In an under-the-radar roster transaction, the Jays have provided an update on 9-year MLB player Joe Mantiply .

More MLB on Heavy: Blue Jays Promote 26-Year-Old Pitcher in Wake of Shane Bieber Injury

Blue Jays Send Joe Mantiply to AAA Buffalo

GettyDETROIT, MICHIGAN – MAY 17: Joe Mantiply #35 of the Toronto Blue Jays pitches the ball against the Detroit Tigers during the bottom of the eighth inning at Comerica Park on May 17, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images)

Per his transactions tracker, Joe Mantiply's rehab assignment has been sent to AAA Buffalo.

MLB.com wrote (on 8/25): "Toronto Blue Jays sent LHP Joe Mantiply on a rehab assignment to Buffalo Bisons."

He has been on the IL since Mid-May with left knee inflammation, but could be returning to the Jays pitching staff shortly.

articles.title: Springfield Cardinals getting new name, logos and uniforms in 2027
articles.summary: SPRINGFIELD, Mo. — The Springfield Cardinals will soon have a new name. The organization announced Tuesday that it will rebrand following the 2026 Minor Leag...
articles.body:
SPRINGFIELD, Mo. — The Springfield Cardinals will soon have a new name.

The organization announced Tuesday that it will rebrand following the 2026 Minor League Baseball season, ending more than two decades under the Springfield Cardinals name.

Beginning in 2027, the team will have a new name, logos and uniforms. The franchise will remain in Springfield, continue playing at Route 66 Stadium and remain the Double-A affiliate of the St. Louis Cardinals .

The new identity has already been selected, according to the team, but fans will have to wait a little longer to find out what it is.

The organization plans to unveil the new name, logos and uniforms during a free launch party at Route 66 Stadium on Tuesday, Oct. 6. Additional details will be announced later.

The Springfield Cardinals have played in the city since 2005. The organization said the change intended to give the team an identity more closely connected to Springfield and southwest Missouri.

articles.title: Francisco Lindor leads resurgent Mets to 3-2 victory over MLB-best Brewers in 10 innings
articles.summary: Francisco Lindor made a diving catch at shortstop with the bases loaded in the ninth inning and scored the winning run on a throwing error in the 10th to lea...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Francisco Lindor made a diving catch at shortstop with the bases loaded in the ninth inning and scored the winning run on a throwing error in the 10th to lead the New York Mets past the Milwaukee Brewers 3-2 on Tuesday night.

Lindor and Luis Robert Jr. homered for the last-place Mets (60-72), who are 13-6 since selling big at the trade deadline. Lindor's homer was his 154th for New York, tying Dave Kingman for sixth on the franchise list.

Carson Benge had his 11th three-hit game for the Mets, most among major league rookies.

With the Mets resting a couple of high-leverage relievers in their revamped bullpen, Austin Warren was summoned in the ninth to protect a 2-1 advantage. He gave up a leadoff double to William Contreras and a tying double to pinch-hitter Christian Yelich that left runners at second and third with nobody out.

But the major league-leading Brewers (81-51) were never able to push across the go-ahead run. With the bases loaded and two outs, David Hamilton hit a line drive off left-hander Jefry Yan that Lindor snagged on his backhand with a dive to his right.

A fired-up Yan pounded the turf and Lindor shouted in celebration — but then Lindor got picked off first base by closer Trevor Megill to end the bottom of the ninth.

Jonathan Pintaro (2-0) stranded two in a hitless 10th, and Megill loaded the bases with one out in the bottom half on an intentional walk to Benge and an unintentional one to Robert.

Christopher Morel hit a grounder wide of third, and Lindor scored when Hamilton's throw to the plate was wild.

Mets starter Zac Thornton allowed one run and seven hits in six innings. Fellow rookie Nate Lavender extended his career-opening scoreless streak to 9 2/3 innings by retiring all six batters he faced before giving way to Warren, whose only big league save came as an Angels rookie in 2021.

Luis Lara had an RBI single for Milwaukee, which finished 2 for 14 with runners in scoring position. Contreras went 3 for 4 with a walk, and starter Kyle Harrison permitted one run over five innings.

Brewers RHP Dustin May (6-8, 4.57 ERA) starts the middle game of the series Wednesday night against RHP Robert Stock (0-2, 5.40).
